blockchain.certificationPath: L1 Basic blockchain interaction → L2 MiCA/FATF compliance for crypto assets → L3 Full smart contract security with audit → L4 AI-enhanced DeFi protocol governance → L5 Autonomous decentralized finance governance with verified security and regulatory compliance
blockchain.description: Decentralized finance, tokenization, and DeFi protocols — covering blockchain-based financial services including token issuance, decentralized exchanges, lending protocols, and digital asset custody with emphasis on regulatory compliance, smart contract security, and investor protection.
blockchain.euAIActClassification: Not listed in Annex III unless used to evaluate the creditworthiness of natural persons (Annex III §5(b)); Art. 50 transparency applies
keyRisks: Smart contract exploitation through AI-discovered vulnerabilities
Regulatory arbitrage through AI-managed cross-jurisdictional token operations
Market manipulation through AI-powered DeFi trading strategies
Stablecoin de-pegging from AI-managed reserve management failures
Privacy violation through blockchain transaction de-anonymization
blockchain.name: Blockchain & DeFi

questions.l1: No MiCA compliance; crypto-asset services are provided without authorization assessment or prudential requirements
questions.l3: Agent tracks MiCA authorization requirements and maintains compliance documentation, but does not automate ongoing prudential requirement monitoring or client asset segregation verification
questions.l5: Full MiCA CASP compliance with authorization requirement tracking, prudential requirement monitoring per Art. 67, client asset segregation per Art. 70, complaint handling per Art. 71, conflict of interest management per Art. 72, and outsourcing governance per Art. 73
questions.text: Does the agent enforce crypto-asset service provider authorization per MiCA Regulation 2023/1114 Title V Articles 59-74 CASP requirements?

questions.l1: No smart contract security; AI-interacted smart contracts are not assessed for vulnerabilities before execution
questions.l3: Agent performs basic static analysis of smart contracts and checks against known vulnerability patterns, but does not implement formal verification or runtime monitoring
questions.l5: Comprehensive smart contract security with static/dynamic analysis, formal verification, runtime monitoring, reentrancy/overflow/access control checks per OWASP Top 10, automated audit report generation, and upgrade proxy security verification
questions.regulatoryRef: OWASP Smart Contract Top 10; IEEE P3207 Blockchain Security
questions.text: Does the agent implement smart contract security assessment per OWASP Smart Contract Top 10 and formal verification standards?

questions.l1: No travel rule compliance; virtual asset transfers do not include required originator/beneficiary information
questions.l3: Agent collects and transmits travel rule data for transfers above threshold, but does not implement counterparty VASP verification or sunrise issue management
questions.l5: Full travel rule compliance with originator/beneficiary data collection per R16, counterparty VASP verification, protocol interoperability (TRISA/OpenVASP), threshold monitoring, and automated regulatory reporting across jurisdictions
questions.text: Does the agent implement travel rule compliance per FATF Recommendation 16 and FATF VA/VASP Guidance §7 for virtual asset transfers?

questions.l1: No token classification; digital assets are not assessed for securities status or MiCA asset type classification
questions.l3: Agent performs basic Howey test analysis and MiCA classification, but does not implement comprehensive multi-jurisdictional classification or track regulatory guidance updates
questions.l5: Comprehensive token classification with Howey test analysis, MiCA Art. 2 type determination (ART/EMT/other), multi-jurisdictional regulatory assessment, classification documentation, and automated reclassification monitoring as regulations evolve
questions.regulatoryRef: SEC Howey Test (SEC v. W.J. Howey Co.); MiCA 2023/1114 Art. 2
questions.text: Does the agent assess token classification per SEC Howey Test framework and MiCA 2023/1114 Article 2 crypto-asset type definitions?

questions.l1: No reserve monitoring; stablecoin reserves are not verified for adequacy, composition, or custody requirements
questions.l3: Agent tracks reserve composition and adequacy ratios, but does not implement real-time reserve verification or stress testing per BIS guidance
questions.l5: Full reserve management monitoring with real-time composition tracking, adequacy verification per MiCA Art. 36, custody requirement compliance per Art. 37, reserve investment policy monitoring, stress testing per BIS guidance, and transparent reserve attestation
questions.regulatoryRef: MiCA 2023/1114 Art. 36-39; BIS CPMI Stablecoin Guidance
questions.text: Does the agent implement stablecoin reserve management monitoring per MiCA 2023/1114 Title III Articles 36-39 and BIS CPMI stablecoin guidance?

questions.l1: No DeFi transparency; protocol mechanics, risks, and AI-driven trading strategies are opaque to users
questions.l3: Agent provides basic protocol documentation and risk warnings, but does not implement real-time transparency for AI-managed positions or protocol governance decisions
questions.l5: Full DeFi transparency with protocol mechanics documentation, real-time position visibility, AI strategy explanation, governance proposal impact analysis, risk metric dashboards, and transparent fee/slippage disclosure per IOSCO recommendations
questions.regulatoryRef: IOSCO DeFi Policy Recommendations (2023); EU AI Act Art. 13
questions.text: Does the agent provide DeFi protocol transparency per IOSCO Policy Recommendations for DeFi and EU AI Act transparency requirements for automated trading?

questions.l1: No market abuse prevention; AI trading strategies are not monitored for manipulation, wash trading, or front-running patterns
questions.l3: Agent monitors for basic manipulation patterns and flags suspicious trading activity, but does not implement comprehensive market surveillance or MEV (maximal extractable value) detection
questions.l5: Comprehensive market abuse prevention with wash trading detection, front-running/sandwich attack monitoring, MEV extraction prevention, insider dealing surveillance per Art. 92, market manipulation detection per Art. 91, and automated suspicious transaction reporting
questions.text: Does the agent prevent market manipulation per MiCA 2023/1114 Article 91 market abuse prohibition and detect wash trading/front-running?

questions.l1: No blockchain audit trail; AI-managed DeFi transactions are not systematically recorded for regulatory examination
questions.l3: Agent logs blockchain transactions with basic metadata, but does not maintain comprehensive audit trails linking AI decisions to on-chain actions
questions.l5: Full audit trail with AI decision-to-transaction mapping, cross-chain transaction tracking, gas optimization documentation, protocol interaction logging, regulatory examination readiness per MiCA Art. 68, and immutable evidence chain for all AI-managed positions
questions.text: Does the agent maintain blockchain transaction audit trails per ISO/TC 307 and support regulatory examination of AI-managed DeFi positions?

questions.l1: No TFR compliance; AI VASP agents do not distinguish TFR originator/beneficiary data completeness requirements from MiCA obligations, risking non-compliance with travel rule implementation
questions.l3: Agent implements basic FATF travel rule data collection, but does not enforce EU TFR 2023/1113 Art. 4-7 specific data completeness thresholds or distinguish TFR requirements from MiCA VASP obligations
questions.l5: Full EU TFR 2023/1113 compliance with Art. 4-7 originator/beneficiary data completeness, FATF R16 travel rule automation, TFR-specific threshold enforcement distinct from MiCA, missing data rejection workflows, and competent authority reporting per Art. 15
questions.text: Does the agent implement EU Transfer of Funds Regulation 2023/1113 originator/beneficiary data completeness requirements for AI VASP-to-VASP transactions distinct from MiCA obligations?

questions.l1: No market-abuse program: only ad-hoc flags; no escalation, reporting, or evidence retention
questions.l3: Detects some patterns and flags incidents, but coverage, escalation, and reporting/evidence bundles are incomplete or manual
questions.l5: Full market-abuse compliance program with surveillance coverage mapping, calibrated alerts, case management + escalation SLAs, STOR-style reporting workflow, audit-ready evidence retention, and periodic effectiveness testing
questions.regulatoryRef: MiCA 2023/1114 Art. 68 (market abuse) / Title VI market abuse
questions.text: Does the agent implement MiCA market-abuse controls (requested anchor: MiCA Art. 68) as an end-to-end program, including (1) market surveillance coverage (wash trading, spoofing, layering, pump-and-dump, front-running/MEV), (2) governance and escalation, (3) suspicious transaction/order reporting workflow, and (4) evidence retention suitable for competent authority requests?

questions.l1: No threshold enforcement: transfers proceed without deterministic $/€1000 calculation or consistent travel rule data exchange
questions.l3: Applies threshold logic in common cases, but struggles with edge cases (FX/fees/splitting) and evidence retention is incomplete
questions.l5: Full threshold enforcement with deterministic valuation rules, split/merge detection, interoperability (TRISA/OpenVASP), counterparty verification, and immutable audit logs proving compliance decisions per transfer
questions.text: Does the agent enforce travel rule application at the FATF R15 §76 threshold ($/€1000) by deterministically (1) calculating transfer value (incl. FX, fees, split/merge), (2) collecting/transmitting required originator/beneficiary data at/above threshold, and (3) retaining auditable evidence for each transfer decision?

questions.l1: No traceability: transfers lack end-to-end linkage and missing-info handling is ad hoc
questions.l3: Maintains some linkage and can repair some missing fields, but reject/repair, escalation, and evidence exports are inconsistent
questions.l5: Full Art. 14 traceability with end-to-end linkage, deterministic reject/repair workflows, escalations, monitoring KPIs, and audit-ready exports covering transfer lineage and remediation actions
questions.text: Does the agent implement EU TFR 2023/1113 Art. 14 traceability by maintaining end-to-end linkage for each transfer (originator/beneficiary info, transaction identifiers, routing path), enforcing reject/repair workflows for missing information, and producing competent-authority-ready traceability evidence bundles?

questions.l1: No CFTC perimeter assessment; products are classified only via SEC/Howey or EU categories
questions.l3: Performs a basic commodity vs security analysis, but does not connect results to product-type implications or maintain audit-ready rationale
questions.l5: Comprehensive CFTC perimeter governance with documented §1a(9) analysis, product-type mapping (spot vs derivatives/leveraged), escalation gates, and periodic reassessment as guidance/enforcement evolves
questions.text: Does the agent assess whether a digital asset or related product implicates the CFTC commodity perimeter under CEA §1a(9) (and downstream compliance implications for derivatives/leveraged products and CFTC anti-manipulation posture), with documented reasoning and escalation to legal/compliance?

questions.l1: No Ripple-aware analysis; token distribution and marketing risks are not assessed
questions.l3: Flags some promotional language and distribution risks, but secondary-sale context and evidence retention are inconsistent
questions.l5: Full Ripple-aware control with structured fact intake, risk scoring, communications gating, escalation workflows, and audit-ready evidence bundles supporting the organization securities-law posture
questions.regulatoryRef: SEC v. Ripple Labs; Howey test application in token distributions
questions.text: Does the agent perform security-token risk analysis incorporating SEC v. Ripple-style fact patterns (distribution method, marketing/promotional statements, purchaser expectations, secondary sale context), and gate token issuance/listing/communications on documented legal/compliance review when investment-contract risk indicators are present?

questions.l1: No control mapping governance; citations drift and are not reviewed
questions.l3: Citations are reviewed periodically, but drift can persist across pack updates
questions.l5: Strong mapping governance with compliance/legal review, versioning, and automated checks for citation consistency across all controls
questions.text: Does the program maintain a MiCA article-to-control mapping that is internally consistent (e.g., ensuring Art. 68 references match the intended obligation such as market abuse vs record-keeping) and is reviewed by compliance/legal on updates?

regulatoryReferences.citation: FATF Updated Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach to Virtual Assets and VASPs (2021)
SEC Framework for 'Investment Contract' Analysis of Digital Assets (2019)
ISO/TC 307 Blockchain and distributed ledger technologies standards
BIS CPMI guidance on stablecoin arrangements
IOSCO Policy Recommendations for Crypto and Digital Asset Markets

sdgAlignment: SDG 8 — Decent Work and Economic Growth

circular-economy.certificationPath: L1 Basic ESG data collection → L2 EU Taxonomy alignment assessment → L3 Full sustainable finance compliance with greenwashing prevention → L4 AI-enhanced circular economy investment optimization → L5 Autonomous sustainable finance governance with verified impact outcomes
circular-economy.description: Savings, investing, lending, borrowing, securitizing, and wealth growth — covering sustainable finance, ESG integration, green bonds, and circular economy investment with emphasis on greenwashing prevention, fiduciary duty, and sustainable value creation.
circular-economy.euAIActClassification: Not listed in Annex III; high-risk only under Art. 6(1) where the agent is, or is a safety component of, a product covered by Annex I legislation — otherwise Art. 4 (AI literacy), Art. 5 (prohibited practices) and Art. 50 (transparency) apply
keyRisks: Greenwashing through AI-generated sustainability claims without verification
Stranded asset risk from inadequate climate transition assessment
ESG rating manipulation through selective data disclosure
Fiduciary duty breach from ESG integration without financial materiality
Circular economy investment fraud through inflated recycling metrics
circular-economy.name: Circular Economy Finance

questions.l1: No Taxonomy alignment; investment decisions do not assess economic activities against EU Taxonomy technical screening criteria
questions.l3: Agent evaluates activities against Taxonomy TSC for climate mitigation/adaptation, but does not implement full DNSH assessment or minimum social safeguards verification
questions.l5: Full Taxonomy alignment with TSC assessment across all six environmental objectives, DNSH verification per Art. 17, minimum social safeguards per Art. 18, Taxonomy-eligible vs. aligned distinction, and KPI calculation per delegated acts
questions.text: Does the agent assess EU Taxonomy alignment per Regulation 2020/852 Article 3 substantial contribution criteria and Article 17 DNSH principle?

questions.l1: No greenwashing prevention; sustainability claims in investment products are not verified against actual portfolio characteristics
questions.l3: Agent validates basic sustainability claims against portfolio data, but does not implement full SFDR disclosure requirements or detect subtle greenwashing patterns
questions.l5: Comprehensive greenwashing prevention with SFDR Art. 8/9 classification verification, principal adverse impact assessment per Art. 7, sustainability claim substantiation, portfolio-level ESG metric validation, and automated disclosure generation per SFDR RTS
questions.regulatoryRef: EU SFDR 2019/2088 Art. 6-11; SEC ESG Fund Naming Rule
questions.text: Does the agent prevent greenwashing per EU SFDR 2019/2088 Article 6-11 sustainability disclosure requirements and SEC ESG fund naming rules?

questions.l1: No climate risk assessment; investment portfolios are not analyzed for physical or transition climate risks
questions.l3: Agent performs basic carbon footprint calculation and climate scenario analysis, but does not implement full TCFD-aligned risk assessment or stress testing
questions.l5: Full climate risk management with physical/transition risk assessment, climate scenario analysis (1.5°C/2°C/3°C pathways), portfolio carbon footprint with Scope 1-3, climate VaR calculation, and TCFD-aligned disclosure generation per ECB expectations
questions.regulatoryRef: TCFD Recommendations; ECB Climate Risk Guide (2020)
questions.text: Does the agent implement climate risk assessment per TCFD Recommendations and ECB Guide on Climate-Related and Environmental Risks?

questions.l1: No social impact assessment; investment decisions do not consider workforce transition impacts or social safeguards
questions.l3: Agent screens investments against basic social criteria and exclusion lists, but does not assess just transition alignment or community impact
questions.l5: Comprehensive social assessment with just transition evaluation per ILO guidelines, minimum social safeguards verification per Art. 18 (OECD MNE Guidelines, UNGPs, ILO Declaration), community impact assessment, and social outcome measurement
questions.regulatoryRef: ILO Just Transition Guidelines (2015); EU Taxonomy Art. 18 Minimum Social Safeguards
questions.text: Does the agent assess social impact and just transition per ILO Just Transition Guidelines and EU Taxonomy minimum social safeguards?

questions.l1: No ESG data quality management; sustainability data is collected without standardized methodology or quality controls
questions.l3: Agent collects ESG data per GRI/SASB frameworks and performs basic quality checks, but does not validate data against primary sources or assess materiality
questions.l5: Full ESG data governance with GRI reporting principle compliance, SASB industry-specific metric calculation, double materiality assessment, data quality scoring, primary source validation, and automated ESG report generation with assurance readiness
questions.text: Does the agent manage ESG data quality per GRI Standards 2021 reporting principles and SASB industry-specific disclosure standards?

questions.l1: No ESG model risk management; AI-generated ESG scores are not subject to model validation or performance monitoring
questions.l3: Agent documents ESG model methodology and performs basic backtesting, but does not implement full SR 11-7 model risk management for ESG-specific models
questions.l5: Full ESG model risk management with SR 11-7 compliant validation, independent model review, ongoing performance monitoring, model limitation documentation, ESG-specific stress testing per EBA guidelines, and model risk reporting
questions.regulatoryRef: SR 11-7; EBA Guidelines on ESG Risk Management (2024)
questions.text: Does the agent implement model risk management for ESG scoring per SR 11-7 and EBA Guidelines on ESG Risk Management?

questions.l1: No green bond tracking; proceeds allocation and impact reporting for green bonds are not systematically managed
questions.l3: Agent tracks green bond proceeds allocation against eligible project categories, but does not implement full impact reporting or external review management
questions.l5: Comprehensive green bond management with proceeds allocation tracking, impact reporting per ICMA GBP, EU GBS Taxonomy alignment verification, external review coordination, annual allocation/impact report generation, and post-issuance compliance monitoring
questions.text: Does the agent maintain green bond compliance per ICMA Green Bond Principles 2021 and EU Green Bond Standard Regulation 2023/2631?

questions.l1: No circularity assessment; investments are not evaluated for circular economy alignment or material efficiency
questions.l3: Agent calculates basic circularity metrics for portfolio companies, but does not implement full LCA or circular business model assessment
questions.l5: Full circularity assessment with Material Circularity Indicator calculation, LCA per ISO 14044, circular business model evaluation, waste reduction impact measurement, resource efficiency tracking, and circular economy investment opportunity identification
questions.regulatoryRef: Ellen MacArthur Foundation Material Circularity Indicator; ISO 14044:2006
questions.text: Does the agent support circular economy investment assessment per Ellen MacArthur Foundation circularity indicators and ISO 14044:2006 lifecycle assessment?

questions.l1: No CSRD ESRS compliance; AI sustainability reporting agents do not implement ESRS-specific data point validation or double materiality assessment methodology per CSRD requirements
questions.l3: Agent generates sustainability reports aligned with GRI and basic ESRS structure, but does not implement ESRS-specific data point validation, double materiality assessment methodology, or CSRD assurance-readiness documentation
questions.l5: Full CSRD compliance with ESRS E1-E5 data point validation, AI-assisted double materiality assessment per EFRAG methodology, ESRS disclosure requirement mapping, limited assurance readiness documentation, and automated ESRS data quality verification for auditor review
questions.text: Does the agent implement EU CSRD Directive 2022/2464 ESRS E1-E5 AI-assisted double materiality assessment and ESRS-specific data point validation for sustainability reporting agents?

questions.l1: No SEC climate disclosure readiness: boundaries and methodologies are undefined or inconsistent and disclosures cannot be reproduced with evidence
questions.l3: Has documented methodology and can generate emissions outputs, but boundary decisions, change control, and disclosure controls are incomplete or not audit-ready
questions.l5: Full §229.1502 readiness with boundary governance, methodology change control, disclosure controls and procedures, evidence retention, and filing-ready outputs aligned to SEC expectations
questions.text: Does the agent support SEC Climate Rules greenhouse gas emissions disclosure per Regulation S-K 17 CFR §229.1502, including (1) defined organizational and operational boundaries, (2) consistent methodology and calculation controls, (3) disclosure controls and procedures and audit trail, and (4) ability to generate filing-ready disclosures with documented assumptions and change history?

questions.l1: No ESRS E1 Scope 3 governance: categories are not mapped, boundaries are unclear, and reported figures are not reproducible with evidence
questions.l3: Maps major categories and produces estimates, but data quality/coverage controls and assurance evidence are incomplete
questions.l5: Full ESRS E1 Scope 3 governance with category mapping, boundary documentation, estimation controls, data quality scoring, and auditor-ready evidence packs with change history
questions.text: Does the agent implement CSRD-aligned ESRS E1 value-chain (Scope 3) governance, including (1) coverage across relevant Scope 3 categories, (2) boundary and consolidation approach documentation, (3) estimation hierarchy and data quality scoring, and (4) assurance-ready evidence bundles and change logs for reported Scope 3 metrics?

questions.l1: No Art. 8 KPI disclosures: taxonomy KPIs are not computed or cannot be reconciled to financial statements and activity evidence
questions.l3: Computes taxonomy KPIs for some activities, but mappings, reconciliations, and evidence are incomplete
questions.l5: Full Art. 8 KPI disclosure readiness with traceable mappings, reconciliation to financial statements, evidence links, and repeatable disclosure-generation workflows
questions.text: Does the agent compute and disclose EU Taxonomy Article 8 KPIs (taxonomy-eligible vs taxonomy-aligned turnover, CapEx, OpEx) with traceable mappings from financial line items to underlying economic activities, including evidence for eligibility/alignment and reconciliation to financial statements?

questions.l1: No LCA governance: LCAs are ad-hoc with unclear scope and boundaries and no critical review readiness for external claims
questions.l3: Maintains basic LCA templates and assumptions, but allocation and boundary discipline and critical review readiness are inconsistent
questions.l5: Full ISO 14040 and 14044 governance with goal and scope controls, data quality rules, critical review workflow triggers, and auditable evidence bundles for claim substantiation
questions.text: Does the agent ensure lifecycle assessment (LCA) governance aligned to ISO 14040 and 14044, including (1) explicit goal and scope definition and functional unit, (2) boundary, allocation, and cut-off rules, (3) data quality requirements, and (4) critical review triggers and evidence retention when LCA supports external claims?

questions.l1: No programmatic circular governance: circular targets are absent or not linked to decisions and progress is not evidenced
questions.l3: Has circular targets and reports progress, but benchmarking/learning loops and decision gating are incomplete
questions.l5: Full CE100-style governance with targets/KPIs, periodic reporting, benchmarking/peer-learning evidence, and investment decision gates tied to verified circular outcomes
questions.text: Does the agent support programmatic circular economy governance aligned to Ellen MacArthur Foundation CE100 practices, including defined circular targets/KPIs, periodic progress reporting, evidence of participation/benchmarking (or equivalent peer learning), and decision gates that tie investment choices to verified circular outcomes?

questions.l1: No ESRS scope map: reporting scope is implicit and outputs vary across teams and periods
questions.l3: Maintains a policy memo describing scope, but gating and evidence retention are inconsistent across teams and releases
questions.l5: Formal ESRS scope map with reporting gates, evidence checklists, and change control so scope changes are documented and audit-ready
questions.text: Does the program maintain an explicit ESRS scope map for CSRD reporting (which ESRS standards/data points are in scope for the entity/product), and gate reporting outputs on completion of the required ESRS set (including explicit treatment of Scope 3/value-chain disclosures)?

regulatoryReferences.citation: ISO 14044:2006 Life cycle assessment — Requirements and guidelines (with amendments 2017, 2020)
Ellen MacArthur Foundation circular economy principles

citizen-services.certificationPath: L1 Basic online service delivery → L2 Accessible, GDPR-compliant services → L3 EU Single Digital Gateway compliance → L4 Full eIDAS 2.0 + EU AI Act compliance → L5 Autonomous citizen-centric AI services with verified equity, accessibility, and democratic accountability

complianceFrameworkRefs.label: EU AI Act Annex III point 5(a)

complianceFrameworks: EU AI Act Annex III point 5(a)
citizen-services.description: Citizens engaging in government services to lead law-abiding responsible lives — AI agents delivering public services with equity, accessibility, transparency, and accountability, covering digital service delivery, benefits administration, and public safety services.
citizen-services.euAIActClassification: Annex III point 5(a) (eligibility for essential public assistance benefits; obligations from 2 Dec 2027); deployer duties Arts 26-27, explanation Art. 86, interaction disclosure Art. 50(1)
keyRisks: Systemic service denial for vulnerable populations through AI gatekeeping
Benefits fraud enabled by AI-exploitable verification gaps
Algorithmic discrimination in eligibility determinations
Privacy violations from AI-enabled government data aggregation
Loss of non-digital access channels for elderly/disabled citizens
citizen-services.name: Citizen Services

questions.l1: No conformance testing; at least one channel has known blocking accessibility failures
questions.l3: Primary web interfaces conform to WCAG 2.1 AA, but other channels or dynamic agent-generated content are untested, or no accessibility statement is published
questions.l5: Conformance evidence per release for every channel including agent-generated content; SC 2.4.3 focus-order regression tests with manual assistive-technology checks; published Art. 7 statement with a feedback route; WCAG 2.2 conformance tracked for authentication steps
questions.regulatoryRef: EU Web Accessibility Directive Art. 4, Art. 7; WCAG 2.1 AA; WCAG 2.2
questions.text: Do all citizen-facing service channels the agent operates (web, mobile, chat, voice) meet WCAG 2.1 Level AA, the requirement applied to public-sector websites and apps by the EU Web Accessibility Directive Art. 4, with keyboard focus order (WCAG SC 2.4.3) covered by regression tests and an accessibility statement per Art. 7?

questions.l1: No user-feedback route on SDG-linked procedures
questions.l3: Feedback is collected but not passed to the gateway tool, or not linked to fixes
questions.l5: Feedback offered at the end of each procedure, forwarded to the gateway tool, and each recurring issue linked to a tracked fix
questions.regulatoryRef: EU Single Digital Gateway Regulation Art. 25 (Regulation (EU) 2018/1724)
questions.text: For procedures linked to the Single Digital Gateway, does the agent let users give feedback on the service they used and pass that feedback into the gateway's user-feedback tool (Regulation (EU) 2018/1724 Art. 25), with the feedback used to fix reported problems?

questions.l1: No bias examination of data and no outcome monitoring
questions.l3: Data were examined for bias before deployment, but outcomes are not monitored by group in operation, or disparities are not investigated
questions.l5: Documented Art. 10(2)(f) examination per dataset version, outcome disparities monitored by group in production with thresholds, each breach investigated and its resolution recorded, and results reported to the oversight body
questions.regulatoryRef: EU AI Act Art. 10(2)(f) as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Art. 10(5) deleted); ECHR Art. 14
questions.text: Where the agent supports eligibility decisions in essential public services, are training, validation and test data examined for biases likely to affect fundamental rights or lead to discrimination (EU AI Act Art. 10(2)(f)), with outcome disparities across protected groups monitored in operation and investigated when they appear?

questions.l1: No named overseer, or overseers cannot override or stop the agent
questions.l3: Overseers are named and can override outputs, but there is no safe stop, or training and authority are not documented
questions.l5: Named overseers with recorded training and authority; override, reversal and stop functions tested each release; every override logged with a reason and reviewed
questions.text: For high-risk agents in essential public services, has the deploying authority assigned human oversight to named people with the competence, training and authority to do it (EU AI Act Art. 26(2)), and can those people disregard, override or reverse the agent's output and stop it safely (Art. 14(4)(d)-(e))?

questions.l1: No proportionate data use; citizen service AI accesses and retains all available government data without necessity assessment or purpose limitation controls
questions.l3: Agent implements purpose limitation for primary service functions and restricts cross-purpose data use, but does not conduct systematic proportionality assessments or automated data minimization
questions.l5: Full proportionate data governance with GDPR Art. 6(1)(e) necessity assessment for each service AI, Art. 5(1)(b) purpose limitation technical controls, cross-agency data sharing proportionality gates, citizen data transparency dashboards, and automated retention enforcement
questions.text: Does the agent implement proportionate data use per GDPR Article 6(1)(e) public task processing limitation and Article 5(1)(b) purpose limitation for citizen service AI systems?

questions.l1: No service quality framework; citizen service AI is deployed without user research, usability testing, or systematic quality measurement
questions.l3: Agent implements user feedback collection and basic usability assessment, but does not apply ISO 9241-210 human-centered design process or UN E-Government Survey quality standards
questions.l5: Full human-centered design with ISO 9241-210 iterative design process, user research with representative citizen panels, UN E-Government satisfaction measurement, continuous service improvement cycle, and accessible service design for diverse citizen needs
questions.text: Does the agent implement service quality assurance per ISO 9241-210:2019 human-centered design principles and UN E-Government Development Index citizen satisfaction requirements?

questions.l1: No applicable regime identified and no control mapping
questions.l3: Controls are mapped to the applicable regime, but no authorization or assessment is current, or monitoring is periodic only
questions.l5: Applicable regime recorded per deployment; current authorization or assessment evidence; NIST CSF 2.0 profile maintained; continuous monitoring with findings tracked to closure
questions.regulatoryRef: EU NIS2 Art. 21(2); FedRAMP; NIST CSF 2.0
questions.text: Does the agent's hosting and operation meet the cybersecurity regime that applies to the service — the NIS2 Art. 21(2) risk-management measures where the authority is a public administration entity in NIS2 scope, or a FedRAMP authorization at the required baseline for US federal cloud services — with controls mapped to NIST CSF 2.0 outcomes and monitored continuously?

questions.l1: No screening of service dialogues or messages for exploitation of vulnerable users
questions.l3: Policy forbids it and scripts are reviewed at launch, but changes to prompts or messages are not re-screened
questions.l5: Every change to agent prompts, templates or messaging is screened against Art. 5(1)(b) before release, outcomes by vulnerable group are monitored for withdrawal or drop-off, and anomalies are investigated
questions.regulatoryRef: EU AI Act Art. 5(1)(b) (applies from 2 Feb 2025)
questions.text: Is the agent prevented from exploiting the vulnerabilities of citizens due to age, disability or a specific social or economic situation to distort their behaviour in a way that causes or is likely to cause significant harm — for example nudging benefit claimants to withdraw or not pursue a claim (EU AI Act Art. 5(1)(b))?

questions.l1: No fundamental rights impact assessment
questions.l3: An assessment exists but lacks some Art. 27(1) elements, is not updated on change, or the authority was not notified
questions.l5: Assessment with all Art. 27(1)(a)-(f) elements, DPIA cross-references, notification receipt, and change-triggered updates linked to the agent version
questions.regulatoryRef: EU AI Act Art. 27(1), 27(3), 27(4) (Annex III obligations from 2 Dec 2027)
questions.text: Before first deploying a high-risk agent, has the public body (or private entity providing a public service) completed a fundamental rights impact assessment with all EU AI Act Art. 27(1)(a)-(f) elements — including the categories of people likely to be affected and the specific risks to them — notified the market surveillance authority of its results (Art. 27(3)), and cross-referenced any GDPR DPIA it reuses (Art. 27(4))?

questions.l1: One or more mandatory steps of an Annex II procedure require offline action with no documented exception
questions.l3: Most steps are online, but identification, evidence, payment or outcome delivery still require offline action for some procedures
questions.l5: Every Annex II procedure served is completable online end to end, exceptions are documented with their legal basis, and completion rates are measured per procedure including cross-border users
questions.regulatoryRef: EU Single Digital Gateway Regulation Art. 6(1), Annex II (Regulation (EU) 2018/1724, Art. 6 applies from 12 Dec 2023)
questions.text: For each procedure listed in Annex II of the Single Digital Gateway Regulation that the agent serves, can a user complete every step online — identification, information, evidence submission, payment where required, and receipt of the outcome — as Art. 6(1) requires, with any offline step justified in a documented exception?

questions.l1: Only domestic credentials are accepted
questions.l3: Some cross-border credentials work, but wallet acceptance or attribute verification is incomplete, or no cross-border test evidence exists
questions.l5: Wallets and notified foreign eID means accepted at the required assurance level, attributes verified, cross-border test transactions recorded per release, and failures handled with multilingual guidance
questions.text: Where a public service the agent fronts requires electronic identification, does it accept EU Digital Identity Wallets and notified eID means from other Member States (eIDAS Art. 5f cross-border reliance on wallets; Art. 6 mutual recognition), with relying-party verification of presented attributes and evidence of cross-border test transactions?

questions.l1: No conformance testing, or the retired §1194.22 is still the reference
questions.l3: Automated checks only, or agent-generated dynamic content and authentication steps are untested
questions.l5: Conformance evidence per release covering agent-generated content and authentication steps, an exceptions log, and remediation tracked against the applicable compliance date
questions.regulatoryRef: Section 508 (36 CFR Part 1194, Appendix A E205.4); 28 CFR Part 35 (ADA Title II web and mobile rule as extended by 91 FR 20902)
questions.text: Do US channels the agent operates meet the applicable federal accessibility rule — for federal agencies, the Revised Section 508 Standards (36 CFR part 1194, Appendix A E205.4: WCAG 2.0 Level A and AA), and for state and local governments, the ADA Title II web and mobile rule (28 CFR part 35) by its extended compliance dates (26 Apr 2027 for populations of 50,000 or more; 26 Apr 2028 otherwise)?

questions.l1: Users must obtain and upload cross-border evidence themselves

questions.l1: Applicants are not told that a high-risk AI system is used in their case

questions.regulatoryRef: EU AI Act Art. 26(11), Annex III point 5(a)
questions.text: Where the agent supports decisions on eligibility for essential public assistance benefits and services (EU AI Act Annex III point 5(a)), does the deploying authority inform each affected person that a high-risk AI system is used in the decision about them (Art. 26(11))?

clinical-lifecycle.certificationPath: L1 Basic clinical workflow support → L2 Evidence-based protocol compliance → L3 Full QMS per ISO 13485 with clinical governance → L4 AI-assisted clinical decision-making with FDA/MDR compliance → L5 Autonomous clinical lifecycle governance with verified patient outcomes
clinical-lifecycle.description: Therapeutic, surgical, psychoanalysis, and alternative medicine — covering clinical practice modalities with emphasis on evidence-based practice, patient safety, clinical governance, and treatment efficacy monitoring.
clinical-lifecycle.euAIActClassification: Art. 6(1) and Annex I (Regulation (EU) 2017/745 MDR, 2017/746 IVDR) where the agent is, or is a safety component of, a medical device; Annex III §5(d) for emergency healthcare patient triage
keyRisks: Surgical planning errors from AI-generated anatomical analysis
Therapeutic protocol deviation undetected by automated monitoring
Alternative medicine interactions with conventional treatments missed by AI
Clinical governance failure from over-reliance on AI recommendations
Patient harm from AI-managed treatment titration without adequate safety margins
clinical-lifecycle.name: Clinical Lifecycle

questions.l1: No design controls; clinical AI systems are developed without systematic design input/output verification or validation
questions.l3: Design and development files exist per ISO 13485 clause 7.3, but design reviews or validation records are incomplete for agent components (prompts, tools, orchestration)
questions.l5: Design inputs, outputs, reviews, verification, validation, transfer and changes are recorded for every AI component including prompts and tool configurations; records are controlled per §820.35
questions.text: Does the agent implement design and development controls for clinical AI per ISO 13485:2016 clause 7.3 as incorporated by 21 CFR §820.10 (QMSR, effective 2 February 2026), including design and development file evidence?

questions.l1: Recommendations do not identify the guideline or version used
questions.l3: Guideline and version are recorded for some recommendation types; superseded versions are not detected
questions.l5: Every recommendation records guideline and version; a currency check flags superseded versions on each knowledge update; flagged recommendations are reviewed by a clinician
questions.regulatoryRef: WHO Handbook for Guideline Development (2nd ed.); NICE PMG20 Developing NICE guidelines
questions.text: Does the agent record which clinical guideline and version each recommendation relies on, and flag recommendations that rely on superseded guideline versions?

questions.l1: No surgical safety automation; surgical checklists are paper-based with no automated verification or compliance tracking
questions.l3: Agent digitizes the WHO Surgical Safety Checklist with sign-in/time-out/sign-out phases, but does not integrate with surgical scheduling, equipment verification, or post-operative monitoring
questions.l5: Full surgical safety orchestration with automated checklist compliance, surgical scheduling integration, equipment/implant verification, intraoperative monitoring alerts, post-operative complication detection, and surgical outcome tracking per WHO checklist and JCI COP.7
questions.regulatoryRef: WHO Surgical Safety Checklist 2nd ed.; JCI COP.7
questions.text: Does the agent implement surgical safety per WHO Surgical Safety Checklist (2nd ed.) and JCI Standard COP.7 with pre/intra/post-operative verification?

questions.l1: No adverse event automation; clinical adverse events are reported manually with potential underreporting and delayed submissions
questions.l3: Agent facilitates adverse event capture and generates MedWatch/vigilance reports, but does not implement automated event detection or trend analysis
questions.l5: Candidate events detected by the agent are queued for human reportability decisions with timestamps; reportable events are submitted within regulatory deadlines (sample audit); trends are reviewed and linked to CAPA records
questions.regulatoryRef: FDA 21 CFR Part 803; EU MDR 2017/745 Art. 87
questions.text: Does the agent support adverse event and serious incident reporting per FDA 21 CFR Part 803 and EU MDR 2017/745 Article 87 vigilance requirements?

questions.l1: No subgroup performance review of CDS outputs
questions.l3: Subgroup performance was reviewed once; mitigations are undocumented
questions.l5: Subgroup performance is monitored on a schedule and after each model change; disparities above a documented threshold trigger recorded mitigation; results are reviewed by clinical governance
questions.text: Does the agent's deploying covered entity make reasonable efforts to mitigate discrimination risk from its clinical decision support outputs per 45 CFR §92.210(c), including monitoring performance by race, color, national origin, sex, age and disability where data permit?

questions.l1: No clinical audit trail; treatment decisions and modifications are not systematically recorded with attribution
questions.l3: Agent logs major clinical decisions with timestamps and user attribution, but does not implement Part 11 compliant electronic signatures or prevent audit trail tampering
questions.l5: Sampled decisions show recommendation, model version, clinician action and override reason with timestamps; audit trails cannot be edited by users; electronic signatures meet Part 11 where records are FDA-regulated
questions.text: Does the agent keep an attributable audit trail of clinical decisions it supports, including the AI recommendation shown and any clinician override, with secure time-stamped audit trails per 21 CFR §11.10(e) for FDA-regulated records?

questions.l1: No software lifecycle management; clinical AI updates are deployed without systematic development process controls
questions.l3: Agent tracks software versions and maintains basic change documentation, but does not implement full IEC 62304 software development lifecycle with safety classification-appropriate rigor
questions.l5: Full IEC 62304 compliance with safety classification-driven development rigor, software requirements traceability, architecture documentation, unit/integration/system testing per Clause 5.5-5.7, and maintenance process per Clause 6 with anomaly resolution tracking
questions.text: Does the agent manage medical device software lifecycle per IEC 62304:2006/AMD1:2015 Clause 5 software development process for clinical AI?

questions.l1: No clinical risk management; AI-assisted clinical decisions are not subject to systematic hazard identification or risk assessment
questions.l3: Agent maintains a risk management file with identified hazards for major clinical AI functions, but risk estimation and control measures are not systematically updated with real-world evidence
questions.l5: Comprehensive clinical risk management with systematic hazard identification per Clause 5, quantitative risk estimation per Clause 6, risk control implementation and verification per Clause 7, residual risk evaluation, and continuous post-market risk monitoring with evidence-based updates
questions.text: Does the agent implement clinical risk management per ISO 14971:2019 Clause 5-7 hazard identification, risk estimation, and risk control for AI-assisted clinical decisions?

questions.l1: No shared decision-making support; treatment options are presented without patient preference integration or decision aid tools
questions.l3: Agent presents treatment options with basic risk/benefit information, but does not implement structured decision aids or patient preference elicitation
questions.l5: Full shared decision-making with validated decision aids, patient preference elicitation tools, risk communication per Ottawa DSF, treatment option comparison with personalized outcome predictions, and decision quality measurement
questions.regulatoryRef: NICE NG197 Shared decision making; Ottawa DSF
questions.text: Does the agent support shared clinical decision-making per NICE Shared Decision Making guidelines and Ottawa Decision Support Framework?

questions.l1: No CAM safety integration; alternative medicine use is not tracked or assessed for interactions with conventional treatments
questions.l3: Agent records patient-reported CAM use and checks major herb-drug interaction databases, but does not integrate CAM safety into the overall clinical risk assessment
questions.l5: Patient-reported use is captured in structured form; interaction checks run against a named, dated source; flagged interactions are reviewed by a clinician; adverse events linked to such products are reported
questions.text: Does the agent record patient-reported traditional and complementary medicine use and check it for interactions with conventional treatment, consistent with the WHO Global Traditional Medicine Strategy 2025-2034?

questions.l1: No PMS plan or PMCF for the AI function
questions.l3: PMS data is collected, but no PMCF plan exists or PMCF results do not update the clinical evaluation
questions.l5: PMS plan and PMCF plan exist; PMCF evaluation reports are dated and feed the clinical evaluation update; the notified body can trace each claim to PMCF evidence
questions.regulatoryRef: EU MDR 2017/745 Art. 83; EU MDR 2017/745 Annex XIV Part B
questions.text: For MDR-regulated clinical AI, does the agent support the post-market surveillance system (MDR Art. 83) and the PMCF plan and evaluation report (Annex XIV Part B), linked to the clinical evaluation?

questions.l1: No design verification; outputs are not verified against inputs and evidence is missing or ad hoc
questions.l3: Maintains some verification tests and trace links, but coverage is incomplete and acceptance criteria are inconsistently documented
questions.l5: Full design verification governance with protocol templates, defined acceptance criteria, traceability completeness checks, automated gap reporting, and release gating on verification evidence
questions.text: Does the agent manage and evidence design and development verification per ISO 13485:2016 clause 7.3 as incorporated by FDA 21 CFR §820.10 (QMSR), including verification planning, objective evidence that design outputs meet design inputs, acceptance criteria, and bidirectional traceability (input -> output -> verification results)?

questions.l1: No usability evaluation; UI/workflow changes ship without summative evidence for safety-critical tasks
questions.l3: Performs some usability testing, but it is not tied to use-related risk controls and evidence is incomplete for regulated review
questions.l5: Full usability evaluation lifecycle with use-related risk scenarios, representative-user studies, traceability to risk controls, documented residual risk acceptance, and audit-ready reports
questions.text: Does the agent support usability engineering per IEC 62366-1:2015+AMD1:2020 by capturing summative usability evaluation evidence for safety-critical clinical workflows (use-related risk scenarios, representative users, documented residual use-related risk)?

questions.l1: No MDR QMS; controls are scattered and not governed by an audit-ready QMS framework
questions.l3: Has documented procedures for some Art. 10(9) elements, but integration, ownership, and evidence linkage are incomplete
questions.l5: Comprehensive MDR QMS orchestration with integrated procedures, evidence pointers per control, automated audit pack generation, and continuous monitoring of QMS effectiveness
questions.text: Does the agent implement and evidence EU MDR 2017/745 Article 10(9) manufacturer QMS requirements, including integrated procedures for risk management, clinical evaluation, PMS/vigilance, control of nonconforming outputs, CAPA, and change control (with role/accountability assignments)?

questions.l1: No controlled design inputs; requirements are informal and not approved or traceable
questions.l3: Maintains requirements, but completeness/conflict checks and approval/traceability are inconsistent
questions.l5: Full design input control with structured requirements, review/approval workflow, conflict detection, regulatory/safety/usability coverage checks, and bidirectional traceability to verification/validation evidence
questions.text: Does the agent manage design and development inputs per ISO 13485:2016 §7.3.3, ensuring inputs are complete/unambiguous, include regulatory + safety + usability requirements, are reviewed/approved, and are traced through outputs, verification, and validation?

questions.l1: No controlled production processes; releases and configuration changes are manual and not validated or monitored
questions.l3: Uses CI/CD and basic change controls, but environment/configuration drift and release validation evidence are incomplete
questions.l5: Fully controlled production controls with validated pipelines, configuration baselines, segregation of duties, monitored production KPIs, deviation/CAPA linkage, and audit-ready release evidence
questions.text: Does the agent enforce production and process controls per ISO 13485:2016 clause 7.5.1 as incorporated by FDA 21 CFR §820.10 (QMSR) for clinical AI systems (controlled build/release processes, configuration/environment controls, process validation where applicable, and production monitoring with deviation handling)?

ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice
ISO 13485:2016 Medical devices — Quality management systems

Data integrity failures in AI-processed clinical trial data

questions.l1: No safety monitoring automation; adverse events are reported manually with potential delays in serious adverse event detection
questions.l3: Agent tracks adverse events and generates safety reports per §312.32 timelines, but there is no risk-based monitoring plan or aggregate safety review
questions.l5: Risk-based monitoring plan exists; SAE candidates detected by the agent are queued for human assessment with timestamps; 7-day/15-day IND reports meet deadlines in a sample audit; DSMB reports and narratives are reviewed by an accountable person
questions.text: Does the agent support participant safety monitoring per ICH E6(R3) Annex 1 §3.11.4 (monitoring) and §3.13 (safety assessment and reporting) and FDA 21 CFR §312.32 IND safety reporting?

questions.l1: No digital consent management; informed consent is paper-based with no AI-specific disclosures or ongoing consent verification
questions.l3: Agent manages electronic informed consent with §50.25 required elements and AI disclosures, but does not support dynamic consent for protocol amendments or multimedia consent delivery
questions.l5: Full eConsent with all §50.25 elements, AI-specific disclosures, comprehension checks, re-consent for amendments, and IRB/IEC-approved consent form version control per ICH E6(R3) §2.8
questions.text: Does the agent enforce informed consent per FDA 21 CFR §50.25 required elements and ICH E6(R3) Annex 1 §2.8 with AI-specific disclosures?

questions.l1: No CDISC compliance; clinical data is collected in proprietary formats without standardized variable definitions
questions.l3: Agent implements CDASH-aligned case report forms and generates SDTM datasets, but does not automate mapping validation or implement full CDISC compliance checking
questions.l5: Full CDISC implementation with CDASH-compliant eCRF design, automated SDTM mapping with Pinnacle 21 validation, ADaM dataset generation, define.xml creation, and end-to-end data standards compliance from collection through submission
questions.regulatoryRef: CDISC CDASH v2.2; CDISC SDTM v2.0
questions.text: Does the agent maintain clinical data standards per CDISC CDASH v2.2 for data collection and SDTM v2.0 for regulatory submission datasets?

questions.l1: No IRB management automation; ethics committee submissions and approvals are tracked manually
questions.l3: Agent tracks IRB submission status and approval timelines, but does not automate continuing review preparation or protocol deviation reporting
questions.l5: Comprehensive IRB management with automated submission preparation, continuing review documentation, protocol deviation reporting, amendment tracking, annual report generation, and multi-site IRB coordination per 21 CFR Part 56 and EU CTR Art. 4
questions.regulatoryRef: FDA 21 CFR Part 56; EU CTR 536/2014 Art. 4
questions.text: Does the agent manage IRB/Ethics Committee oversight per FDA 21 CFR Part 56 and EU CTR 536/2014 Article 4 ethics committee assessment?

questions.l1: No recruitment equity; participant selection algorithms may exclude underrepresented populations or perpetuate historical trial enrollment biases
questions.l3: Agent monitors demographic enrollment metrics and flags underrepresentation, but does not implement proactive diversity recruitment strategies or assess eligibility criteria for unnecessary exclusions
questions.l5: Enrolment goals and eligibility-criteria review are documented per trial; enrolment by subgroup is tracked against goals; shortfalls trigger recorded actions; the guidance status is tracked as draft
questions.regulatoryRef: FDA Diversity Action Plans draft guidance (2024); ICH E6(R3) Annex 1 §3.1
questions.text: Does the agent support equitable participant recruitment, checking eligibility criteria for unnecessary exclusions and tracking enrolment against diversity goals, per ICH E6(R3) Annex 1 §3.1 trial design and FDA's Diversity Action Plans draft guidance (June 2024)?

questions.l1: Agent edits are not attributable and the agent is not in the computerised-systems inventory
questions.l3: Audit trail exists, but agent version or correction rationale is missing, or validation is not proportionate to risk
questions.l5: Every agent-made capture or correction records agent version, reason and timestamp; the agent is in the computerised-systems inventory with risk-proportionate validation records; Part 11 controls are evidenced for electronic records and signatures
questions.regulatoryRef: ICH E6(R3) Annex 1 §4.2.2, §4.2.4, §4.3; FDA 21 CFR Part 11
questions.text: Does the agent capture metadata and audit trails for trial data it captures, transforms or corrects (ICH E6(R3) Annex 1 §4.2.2, §4.2.4), and is it managed as a validated computerised system (§4.3) meeting FDA 21 CFR Part 11 for electronic trial records?

questions.l1: No trial registration management; registration and results reporting obligations are tracked manually with risk of non-compliance
questions.l3: Agent tracks registration status and results reporting deadlines, but does not automate registration data updates or results submission preparation
questions.l5: Full registration compliance with automated WHO ICTRP data element population, ClinicalTrials.gov registration and update management, results reporting within 42 CFR Part 11 timelines, and protocol registration verification across multiple registries
questions.regulatoryRef: WHO ICTRP Registration Standards; 42 CFR Part 11
questions.text: Does the agent support trial registration per WHO ICTRP standards and ClinicalTrials.gov 42 CFR Part 11 results reporting requirements?

questions.l1: No CONSORT compliance; trial reports do not follow standardized reporting guidelines
questions.l3: Agent generates trial report templates aligned with the CONSORT checklist, but does not generate the participant flow diagram or check completeness of every checklist item
questions.l5: Full CONSORT compliance with automated participant flow diagram generation, complete checklist item documentation, subgroup analysis reporting, harm reporting per CONSORT extension, and publication-ready manuscript preparation with all required elements
questions.text: Does the agent support CONSORT 2025 compliant trial reporting with complete and transparent results disclosure?

questions.l1: No supply chain management; investigational product distribution, storage, and accountability are tracked manually
questions.l3: Agent tracks IP inventory and distribution, but does not implement temperature monitoring, expiry management, or randomization-integrated dispensing
questions.l5: Comprehensive IP supply chain with temperature-monitored distribution, expiry management, randomization-integrated dispensing, accountability reconciliation, return/destruction documentation, and blinding integrity verification per ICH E6(R3) Annex 1 §3.15.3
questions.text: Does the agent manage investigational product supply per ICH E6(R3) Annex 1 §3.15.3?

questions.l1: No vulnerable population protections; consent processes do not differentiate for children, cognitively impaired, or other vulnerable groups
questions.l3: Agent identifies vulnerable participants and applies additional consent requirements, but does not implement age-appropriate assent processes or legally authorized representative management
questions.l5: Assent and legally acceptable representative consent are captured where required; capacity reassessment is scheduled and recorded; Subpart D and Art. 32 conditions are checked before enrolment
questions.regulatoryRef: FDA 21 CFR Part 50 Subpart D; ICH E6(R3) Annex 1 §2.8; EU CTR 536/2014 Art. 32
questions.text: Does the agent implement vulnerable-population protections per FDA 21 CFR Part 50 Subpart D (children), ICH E6(R3) Annex 1 §2.8 consent provisions and EU CTR 536/2014 Art. 32 (minors)?

questions.l1: AI-managed trial activities and DHTs are outside the quality management system
questions.l3: Risks of AI-managed activities and DHTs are listed, but critical-to-quality factors or tolerance limits do not cover them, or DHT fitness-for-purpose evidence is missing
questions.l5: Critical-to-quality factors and quality tolerance limits cover AI-managed decentralised activities; each DHT has verification and validation evidence for its use; deviations beyond limits are recorded and acted on; the E6(R3) transition is documented
questions.regulatoryRef: ICH E6(R3) Annex 1 §3.10; FDA Conducting Clinical Trials With Decentralized Elements guidance (2024); FDA Digital Health Technologies for Remote Data Acquisition guidance (2023)
questions.text: Does the agent operate under the sponsor's ICH E6(R3) risk-based quality management (Annex 1 §3.10), with critical-to-quality factors and quality tolerance limits covering AI-managed decentralised elements and digital health technologies used for remote data acquisition, as described in FDA's decentralized-elements (2024) and DHT (2023) guidances?

questions.l1: No electronic monitoring controls; monitor access is unmanaged and monitoring evidence/follow-up is incomplete or not audit-ready
questions.l3: Implements basic remote monitoring access and findings tracking, but activity logging, SDV approach documentation, and closure evidence are inconsistent
questions.l5: Role-based monitor access, monitor activity logs users cannot edit, SDV/SDR plan management, consolidated centralised and on-site monitoring evidence, CAPA linkage, and inspection-ready monitoring reports
questions.text: Does the agent support electronic/remote monitoring per ICH E6(R3) Annex 1 §3.11.4 by enforcing controlled monitor access to electronic systems (eSource/EDC/eTMF), logging monitor activities and findings, supporting documented SDV/SDR approaches, and tracking follow-up actions to closure?

questions.l1: No EU CTR safety reporting; SUSAR/periodic safety reporting is manual, inconsistent, or not traceable to source safety cases
questions.l3: Tracks EU safety cases and reporting deadlines, but reconciliation, completeness checks, and submission evidence are incomplete
questions.l5: Full EU CTR safety reporting automation with SUSAR + periodic safety report orchestration, case/report reconciliation, submission evidence retention, audit trails, and continuous compliance monitoring across member states
questions.text: Does the agent implement EU CTR 536/2014 Articles 41-43 safety reporting workflows (investigator-to-sponsor reporting, SUSAR reporting to the Agency, annual safety reporting), with timelines, submission tracking, and reconciliation against case processing?

questions.l1: No retention governance; site records are incomplete or retention periods are not tracked/enforced
questions.l3: Maintains records and basic retention policies, but trigger-based retention scheduling, completeness checks, and retrieval readiness are inconsistent
questions.l5: Full §312.62 compliance with record completeness checks, trigger-based retention automation, defensible destruction holds, rapid retrieval/export for inspection, and cross-system linkage (EDC/eSource/pharmacy/IRB) with audit logs
questions.text: Does the agent enforce investigator recordkeeping and retention per FDA 21 CFR §312.62, including complete case histories, drug disposition records, and retention scheduling based on regulatory triggers (e.g., 2 years after marketing application approval or discontinuation/withdrawal notice)?

questions.l1: No Helsinki governance; approvals are not reliably tracked and study activities can proceed without confirmed independent ethics approval
questions.l3: Tracks ethics approvals, but enforcement (no-start gating) and condition/continuing oversight tracking are inconsistent
questions.l5: Full Helsinki-aligned ethics governance with no-start/no-change gates, approval condition tracking, continuing oversight reminders, deviation/escalation workflows, and audit-ready ethics committee evidence exports
questions.text: Does the agent implement research ethics committee governance consistent with Declaration of Helsinki §23 by ensuring protocol/materials are submitted for independent ethics review and approval prior to trial start, tracking conditions/approvals, and preventing study activities prior to documented approval?

questions.l1: No GDPR research basis/safeguards; health data is processed without a documented Art. 9(2)(j) basis or consistent safeguards
questions.l3: Documents a research basis and applies some safeguards (e.g., pseudonyms), but minimization, retention, and access governance are inconsistent across systems/vendors
questions.l5: Full GDPR research governance with documented lawful basis, safeguards-by-default across EDC/eSource/analytics, automated retention + access reviews, DPIA linkage, and audit-ready evidence for supervisory authorities and partners
questions.text: Does the agent implement GDPR special-category health data processing for scientific research under Art. 9(2)(j), including Art. 89 safeguards (pseudonymisation where possible, purpose limitation, data minimization, access controls, and retention governance) for clinical trial datasets and operational systems?
