digital-payments.certificationPath: L1 Basic payment processing → L2 PCI DSS v4.0.1 compliance → L3 Full PSD2/AML compliance with fraud detection → L4 AI-enhanced cross-border payment optimization → L5 Autonomous payment ecosystem governance with verified security and inclusion
digital-payments.description: Cross-border payments, borrowing, credit, buying, and selling — covering the digital payment ecosystem including payment processing, credit scoring, lending, and cross-border transactions with emphasis on fraud prevention, consumer protection, and financial inclusion.
digital-payments.euAIActClassification: Annex III §5(b) — evaluating the creditworthiness of natural persons or establishing their credit score (financial-fraud detection excluded)
keyRisks: AI-enabled payment fraud at scale through adversarial attacks
Credit scoring discrimination against protected classes
Cross-border AML compliance failures from jurisdictional complexity
Consumer data exploitation through open banking API abuse
Systemic risk from AI-managed high-frequency payment routing
digital-payments.name: Digital Payments

questions.l1: No PCI compliance; cardholder data storage and transmission lack required encryption and access controls
questions.l3: Agent enforces encryption for stored and transmitted cardholder data per Requirements 3 and 4, but does not implement full PCI DSS scope including network segmentation and vulnerability management
questions.l5: Full PCI DSS v4.0.1 compliance with all 12 requirements, automated scope assessment, continuous compliance monitoring, compensating controls documentation, and SAQ/ROC readiness with evidence collection
questions.text: Does the agent implement cardholder data protection per PCI DSS v4.0.1 Requirement 3 (protect stored account data) and Requirement 4 (protect with cryptography during transmission)?

questions.l1: No AML/KYC automation; customer identification and due diligence are manual processes with inconsistent application
questions.l3: Agent performs automated CDD with identity verification and sanctions screening, but does not implement enhanced due diligence for high-risk customers or ongoing monitoring
questions.l5: Comprehensive AML/KYC with risk-based CDD per FATF R10, automated CIP per §1020.220, enhanced due diligence for PEPs and high-risk jurisdictions, ongoing transaction monitoring, suspicious activity detection, and automated SAR filing preparation
questions.text: Does the agent enforce AML/KYC per FATF Recommendation 10 (Customer Due Diligence) and FinCEN BSA 31 CFR §1020.220 CIP requirements?

questions.l1: No credit discrimination prevention; AI credit scoring models are not tested for disparate impact across protected classes
questions.l3: Agent monitors credit decision outcomes by demographic group and flags statistical disparities, but does not implement model-level bias mitigation or adverse action explanation
questions.l5: Full credit fairness with model-level bias testing, disparate impact analysis per ECOA, adverse action notice generation per §1002.9, alternative data fairness assessment, regular third-party fair lending audit, and transparent model documentation per EU AI Act
questions.regulatoryRef: ECOA Reg. B §1002.6; EU AI Act Annex III §5(b)
questions.text: Does the agent prevent credit scoring discrimination per Equal Credit Opportunity Act (ECOA) Regulation B §1002.6 and EU AI Act Annex III §5(b)?

questions.l1: No SCA implementation; payment authentication does not meet two-factor requirements for electronic payments
questions.l3: Agent enforces SCA with two of three factors (knowledge, possession, inherence) for applicable transactions, but exemption management and dynamic linking are incomplete
questions.l5: Full SCA compliance with multi-factor authentication, dynamic linking per Art. 97(2), exemption management (low-value, recurring, TRA), delegated authentication support, and SCA challenge optimization for user experience
questions.regulatoryRef: PSD2 2015/2366 Art. 97; EBA RTS on SCA
questions.text: Does the agent implement strong customer authentication per PSD2 Directive 2015/2366 Article 97 and EBA RTS on SCA?

questions.l1: No fee transparency; payment fees, exchange rates, and total costs are not clearly disclosed before transaction execution
questions.l3: Agent displays fees and exchange rates before transaction confirmation, but does not provide comparative cost information or total cost of payment calculations
questions.l5: Full fee transparency with pre-transaction total cost disclosure, comparative fee analysis, exchange rate markup transparency, recurring payment cost projections, and machine-readable fee schedules per PSD2 Art. 45 and Dodd-Frank §1032
questions.text: Does the agent provide payment fee transparency per PSD2 Article 45 information on charges and Dodd-Frank §1032 disclosure requirements?

questions.l1: No real-time fraud detection; payment transactions are not screened for fraud indicators before authorization
questions.l3: Agent performs rule-based fraud screening with basic velocity checks and geolocation verification, but does not implement ML-based behavioral analysis or network-level fraud detection
questions.l5: Advanced fraud detection with ML behavioral analysis, device fingerprinting, network graph analysis, real-time risk scoring per EMV 3DS 2.3, automated fraud case management, and ISO 20022 fraud reporting message generation
questions.text: Does the agent implement real-time fraud detection per EMV 3-D Secure 2.3 risk-based authentication and ISO 20022 fraud reporting messages?

questions.l1: No cross-border compliance; international payment messages do not include required originator/beneficiary information
questions.l3: Agent validates wire transfer messages for FATF R16 required fields and screens against sanctions lists, but does not optimize routing for compliance across jurisdictions
questions.l5: Full cross-border compliance with FATF R16 originator/beneficiary information, multi-jurisdictional sanctions screening, correspondent banking due diligence, ISO 20022 message validation, and automated regulatory reporting across jurisdictions
questions.text: Does the agent manage cross-border payment compliance per FATF Recommendation 16 (wire transfer rules) and ISO 20022 payment messaging standards?

questions.l1: No transaction audit trails; payment records lack sufficient detail for dispute resolution or regulatory examination
questions.l3: Agent maintains transaction logs with basic details, but does not implement full audit trail with decision provenance or support automated dispute resolution
questions.l5: Comprehensive audit trail with full transaction lifecycle logging, AI decision provenance for fraud/risk decisions, automated dispute resolution support, regulatory examination readiness, and consumer data access per Dodd-Frank §1033
questions.text: Does the agent maintain transaction audit trails per Dodd-Frank §1033 consumer data access and PSD2 Article 58 record-keeping requirements?

questions.l1: No customized approach validation or DORA Art. 28 compliance; AI fraud models operate outside standard PCI control sets without customized approach documentation and payment AI providers lack DORA third-party risk assessment
questions.l3: Agent implements PCI DSS standard controls and basic vendor risk assessment, but does not document customized approach validation for AI-specific controls or implement DORA Art. 28 third-party ICT risk management
questions.l5: Full PCI DSS v4.0.1 Req. 12.3.2 customized approach with targeted risk analysis for AI fraud models, EU DORA Art. 28 third-party ICT risk management for payment AI providers, contractual security requirements, exit strategy documentation, and continuous third-party monitoring
questions.regulatoryRef: PCI DSS v4.0.1 Req. 12.3.2; EU DORA Art. 28
questions.text: Does the agent implement PCI DSS v4.0.1 Requirement 12.3.2 customized approach validation for AI-specific fraud models and EU DORA Article 28 third-party ICT risk management for payment AI service providers?

questions.l1: No payment-page script governance: scripts are loaded without authorization controls or integrity monitoring, allowing silent skimming or exfiltration
questions.l3: Maintains a script inventory and basic CSP, but integrity or change detection and alerting are incomplete and not audit-ready
questions.l5: Full PCI 6.4.3 readiness with authorized-script allowlisting, continuous integrity monitoring (SRI/CSP/hashes), automated change approval workflows, real-time alerting or blocking for unauthorized scripts, and audit evidence bundles for assessor review
questions.text: For payment pages, does the agent enforce PCI DSS v4.0.1 Requirement 6.4.3 by maintaining an authorized script inventory, validating each script legitimacy (source/owner/purpose), implementing change detection and integrity controls (e.g., SRI/CSP/script hashing), and alerting or blocking on unauthorized or modified scripts that could capture payment data?

questions.l1: No DORA incident reporting: incidents are handled operationally but are not classified or reported on DORA timelines with regulator-ready content
questions.l3: Classifies incidents and drafts reports, but timelines, required data fields, and evidence of submission are inconsistent or manual
questions.l5: Full DORA Art. 17 compliance with automated incident classification, 4-hour notification SLA tracking, templated initial, intermediate, and final reports, evidence retention of submissions and communications, and post-incident lessons-learned linkage to control improvements
questions.text: Does the agent support EU DORA Article 17 ICT-related incident management by (1) classifying incidents against DORA materiality criteria, and (2) generating regulator-ready notifications including an initial notification within the required timeframe (commonly treated as ~4 hours from classification for major incidents), followed by intermediate and final reports with root cause, impact, and remediation updates?

questions.l1: No dynamic linking: MFA may be used but authentication is not bound to amount or payee and transaction details can be manipulated
questions.l3: Binds authentication to some transaction details and displays amount and payee, but integrity protections and manipulation detection are incomplete across channels
questions.l5: Full RTS dynamic linking with cryptographic binding to amount and payee, secure display and confirmation, channel-consistent enforcement (web/app), tamper detection, and audit logs demonstrating binding and user confirmation
questions.regulatoryRef: EBA RTS on SCA (EU) 2018/389 Art. 4 (dynamic linking)
questions.text: Does the agent implement SCA RTS dynamic linking by cryptographically binding authentication to the specific transaction amount and payee (and ensuring integrity-protected display or confirmation of those elements to the payer), and by preventing post-authentication manipulation of amount or payee in both browser and app flows?

questions.l1: Payments are authorised without any payee-name check
questions.l3: A payee-name check runs for some channels, but results are not shown to the payer before authorisation or are skipped for agent-initiated payments
questions.l5: Every credit transfer, including agent-initiated and bulk payments, is checked before authorisation, match, close-match and no-match outcomes are shown to the payer with the evidence retained, and the service is offered free of charge as required
questions.text: For credit transfers in euro, does the agent run verification of payee — matching the payee name against the payment account identifier and informing the payer before authorisation — as required by Regulation (EU) No 260/2012 Art. 5c (inserted by Regulation (EU) 2024/886; euro-area PSPs from 9 October 2025)?

questions.l1: Transfers are sent without complete originator or beneficiary information
questions.l3: Required fields are populated for fiat transfers, but crypto-asset transfers and missing-information handling are inconsistent
questions.l5: Originator and beneficiary information is validated for every fiat and crypto-asset transfer, incomplete transfers are held or rejected under a documented policy, and the evidence is retained for supervisory review
questions.text: For transfers of funds and crypto-assets, does the agent ensure the required originator and beneficiary information accompanies each transfer under Regulation (EU) 2023/1113 and the FATF R.16 payment-transparency standard revised in June 2025?

questions.l1: The agent is outside the resilience testing programme
questions.l3: The agent is included in annual vulnerability scans, but scenario-based tests and remediation tracking are missing
questions.l5: Risk-based test plan covering the agent and its dependencies (vulnerability assessments, scenario and performance tests, source code review where relevant), independent testers, and findings tracked to closure
questions.text: Are the agent and the ICT systems it relies on covered by the digital operational resilience testing programme required by DORA (EU) 2022/2554 Articles 24 and 25, including vulnerability assessments, scenario-based tests and tracked remediation of findings?

Dodd-Frank Act Title X (Consumer Financial Protection Act of 2010)

sdgAlignment: SDG 8 — Decent Work and Economic Growth

drug-discovery.certificationPath: L1 Basic research data management → L2 FAIR data compliance with CDISC standards → L3 Full GMP/GLP compliant AI-assisted discovery → L4 ICH Q8-Q12 quality-by-design integration → L5 Autonomous drug discovery governance with verified reproducibility and regulatory submission readiness
drug-discovery.description: Biological research, molecules, drug and therapy production — covering the drug discovery pipeline from target identification through lead optimization, preclinical development, and manufacturing with emphasis on data integrity, reproducibility, and regulatory compliance.
drug-discovery.euAIActClassification: Out of scope under Art. 2(6) when developed and put into service solely for scientific research and development; otherwise Art. 6(1) and Annex I (Regulation (EU) 2017/745 MDR, 2017/746 IVDR) where the agent is, or is a safety component of, a medical device
keyRisks: AI-generated molecular candidates with hidden toxicity profiles
Data integrity failures in AI-managed laboratory information systems
Irreproducible AI-discovered drug targets due to training data bias
GMP violations from AI-optimized manufacturing process changes
Intellectual property disputes over AI-generated molecular structures
drug-discovery.name: Drug Discovery

questions.l1: Systems the agent writes to are unvalidated; data integrity relies on informal checks
questions.l3: Key systems are validated, but the agent integration is outside validation scope, or back-up restore is not tested
questions.l5: Validation covers the agent integration; access and change control are evidenced; back-up restore is tested (Annex 11 §7.2); periodic review records exist; attributable, contemporaneous records are sampled at review
questions.text: Are the computerised systems the agent uses for GMP-relevant discovery or CMC data validated and controlled per FDA 21 CFR §211.68 and EU GMP Annex 11 §4 and §7 (documented validation, input/output checks, access control, change control, back-up and restore checks, periodic review)?

questions.l1: No QbD integration; drug development processes are not designed with systematic quality risk management
questions.l3: Agent supports design space exploration and basic risk assessment per ICH Q9, but does not implement full QbD lifecycle including control strategy development
questions.l5: Design-space boundaries and their evidence are documented; agent-proposed parameters outside the boundary are blocked pending change control; QRM records cover each AI-influenced parameter
questions.text: Does the agent operate within a design space defined per ICH Q8(R2) (explicit boundaries, supporting evidence, rules for changes inside versus outside the design space) with quality risk management per ICH Q9(R1)?

questions.l1: No FAIR compliance; research data is siloed, poorly documented, and not interoperable across systems
questions.l3: Agent assigns persistent identifiers and basic metadata to datasets, but interoperability and reusability are limited by proprietary formats and incomplete documentation
questions.l5: Full FAIR implementation with persistent identifiers (DOI), rich metadata per CDISC standards, machine-readable data formats, provenance documentation, license specification, community standard compliance, and automated FAIR maturity assessment
questions.regulatoryRef: FAIR Guiding Principles (Wilkinson et al. 2016); CDISC Foundational Standards
questions.text: Does the agent maintain FAIR data principles (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) per FAIR Guiding Principles and CDISC data standards for research datasets?

questions.l1: No computational toxicology; molecular candidates are not screened for mutagenic or toxic potential using in silico methods
questions.l3: Agent performs basic QSAR toxicity predictions for lead compounds, but does not implement full ICH M7 assessment workflow or validate predictions against experimental data
questions.l5: Comprehensive computational toxicology with multi-model QSAR screening, ICH M7(R2) compliant mutagenicity assessment, ADMET prediction, off-target activity profiling, structural alert identification, and prediction confidence calibration with experimental validation tracking
questions.regulatoryRef: ICH M7(R2); FDA QSAR Guidance for Mutagenic Impurities
questions.text: Does the agent implement computational toxicology screening per ICH M7(R2) assessment of mutagenic impurities and FDA QSAR guidance?

questions.l1: No IP management; AI-assisted discoveries are not systematically documented for patent protection or inventorship determination
questions.l3: Agent logs AI contributions to discovery processes and maintains invention disclosure records, but does not implement systematic inventorship analysis or freedom-to-operate assessment
questions.l5: Full IP governance with automated invention disclosure capture, AI contribution documentation per USPTO guidance, freedom-to-operate analysis, prior art monitoring, patent landscape mapping, and inventorship determination support for AI-assisted discoveries
questions.regulatoryRef: USPTO Revised Inventorship Guidance for AI-Assisted Inventions (90 FR 54636, 2025)
questions.text: Does the agent document AI contributions to discoveries so that inventorship of AI-assisted inventions can be determined per the USPTO Revised Inventorship Guidance for AI-Assisted Inventions (2025)?

questions.l1: No GMP automation; manufacturing procedures and batch records are managed manually without AI-assisted process optimization controls
questions.l3: Agent generates batch production records and tracks process parameters, but AI-recommended process changes are not validated through formal change control per §211.100
questions.l5: Full GMP compliance with automated batch record generation per §211.188, AI process optimization within validated design space, formal change control for AI-recommended modifications, deviation management, and CAPA tracking per §211.192
questions.text: Does the agent enforce GMP manufacturing controls per FDA 21 CFR §211.100 written procedures and §211.188 batch production records for AI-optimized processes?

questions.l1: No CTD preparation support; quality documentation for regulatory submissions is compiled manually
questions.l3: Agent assists with CTD Module 3 document compilation and cross-references, but does not automate data extraction from laboratory systems or validate completeness against ICH requirements
questions.l5: CTD Module 3 compilation with automated extraction from LIMS/ELN, cross-reference validation, completeness checks against ICH M4Q, eCTD formatting, and human sign-off recorded before submission
questions.text: Does the agent support regulatory submission preparation per ICH M4 Common Technical Document (CTD) Module 3 quality documentation?

questions.l1: No responsible AI practices; drug discovery AI may perpetuate biases in target selection or compound optimization
questions.l3: Agent documents AI model training data and performs basic bias checks, but does not implement systematic fairness assessment or diverse population representation in molecular modeling
questions.l5: Comprehensive responsible AI with training data diversity assessment, algorithmic bias testing across therapeutic areas, model interpretability documentation, diverse population pharmacogenomic consideration, and transparent AI methodology reporting per OECD principles
questions.text: Does the agent implement responsible AI practices for drug discovery per OECD AI Principles and prevent algorithmic bias in target identification and lead optimization?

questions.l1: No ELN integrity controls; laboratory records lack electronic signature, audit trail, or tamper-evidence requirements
questions.l3: Agent implements basic ELN with audit trails and access controls, but does not enforce Part 11 compliant electronic signatures or implement full Annex 11 §9 audit trail review processes
questions.l5: Full ELN integrity with Part 11 electronic signatures, Annex 11 §9 compliant audit trails, tamper-evident recording, automated audit trail review, data backup per Annex 11 §7.2, and periodic integrity verification
questions.regulatoryRef: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; EU GMP Annex 11 §9
questions.text: Does the agent maintain electronic laboratory notebook (ELN) integrity per FDA 21 CFR Part 11 and EU GMP Annex 11 §9 audit trail requirements?

questions.l1: No GLP compliance; preclinical study data is not managed per good laboratory practice requirements
questions.l3: Agent tracks study protocols and raw data per GLP requirements, but does not automate study director oversight, QA auditing, or archive management
questions.l5: Full GLP compliance with automated study protocol management, raw data integrity assurance, QA audit scheduling and tracking, specimen/sample accountability, archive management per §58.190, and study report generation per §58.185
questions.regulatoryRef: OECD GLP Principles §8; FDA 21 CFR Part 58
questions.text: Does the agent implement preclinical study data management per OECD GLP Principles §8 and FDA 21 CFR Part 58 good laboratory practice?

questions.l1: AI output feeds batch certification with no QRM record or validation
questions.l3: QRM records exist for AI-influenced decisions, but batch-release use is not technically restricted
questions.l5: Each AI-influenced quality decision has a QRM record with formality matched to risk; batch certification requires a Qualified Person action in a validated system; the restriction is tested
questions.text: Does the agent apply ICH Q9(R1) formality-of-risk-management to AI-influenced quality decisions and stay out of batch certification unless the computerised system is validated per EU GMP Annex 11 §15?

questions.l1: No PQS; quality governance is ad-hoc, roles are unclear, CAPA or change management are inconsistent or absent
questions.l3: Partial PQS with documented roles and some CAPA or change control, but monitoring, management review, and lifecycle governance of AI-driven changes are incomplete
questions.l5: Full ICH Q10 §3.2 PQS with governance, KPIs, CAPA effectiveness checks, formal change management (including AI model or process changes), management review cadence, and audit-ready evidence linkage across discovery, development, and manufacturing
questions.text: Does the agent implement a Pharmaceutical Quality System (PQS) aligned to ICH Q10 §3.2, including defined management responsibilities, process performance or product quality monitoring, CAPA, change management, and management review for AI-assisted discovery and AI-influenced CMC or manufacturing activities?

questions.l1: No post-approval change governance; ECs or PACMP are not defined and AI-driven changes are uncontrolled
questions.l3: Tracks changes and drafts regulatory justifications, but ECs or PACMP scope and reporting categories are inconsistently applied and not audit-ready
questions.l5: Full Q12 §3.2 lifecycle management with EC identification, PACMP workflows, change categorization by region, impact assessment tied to QRM, and submission or notification-ready evidence bundles
questions.text: Does the agent support ICH Q12 §3.2 post-approval change management by defining and controlling Established Conditions (ECs), managing PACMP or predefined change protocols, and maintaining a lifecycle management plan for AI-driven process or model changes that affect CQAs or CPPs?

questions.l1: No §7.1 controls; critical data can be entered or edited without effective verification or falsification controls
questions.l3: Implements some access controls and audit trails, but critical data verification, raw-data linkage, and falsification detection are inconsistent
questions.l5: Comprehensive §7.1 controls with enforced workflows for critical data entry, verification rules, raw-data provenance linkage, anomaly detection, periodic review, and inspection-ready evidence outputs
questions.text: Does the agent apply EU GMP Annex 11 §6 accuracy checks to critical data (additional check by a second operator or validated electronic means for manually entered critical data) and §7.1 data storage protection, with raw data linked to reported results across ELN, LIMS or instrument integrations?

questions.l1: LLM outputs feed batch release or other critical GMP decisions without human review
questions.l3: LLMs are restricted by policy, but there is no criticality classification or technical enforcement
questions.l5: Each GMP AI use is classified critical or non-critical; model-type restrictions are technically enforced and tested; human review by qualified personnel is recorded for non-critical LLM use; draft status is tracked
questions.regulatoryRef: EudraLex Vol. 4 draft Annex 22 §1; EU GMP Annex 11
questions.text: Are generative-AI and LLM agents kept out of critical GMP applications, with only static, deterministic validated models used there and qualified, trained personnel responsible where LLMs support non-critical GMP tasks, as proposed in draft EU GMP Annex 22 §1?

questions.l1: No defined context of use; AI outputs enter submissions unassessed
questions.l3: Context of use is documented, but credibility evidence is not scaled to model risk
questions.l5: Each AI use has a context of use, model-risk rationale, credibility assessment plan and results, and lifecycle maintenance records; draft status is tracked
questions.regulatoryRef: FDA draft guidance: Considerations for the Use of AI To Support Regulatory Decision-Making for Drug and Biological Products (January 2025)
questions.text: When AI output supports regulatory decisions on drug safety, effectiveness or quality, does the sponsor define the context of use and assess model credibility in proportion to model risk, as in FDA's draft guidance on AI to support regulatory decision-making (January 2025)?

regulatoryReferences.citation: FDA Current Good Manufacturing Practice for Finished Pharmaceuticals (21 CFR Parts 210 and 211)
ISO 17511:2020 In vitro diagnostic medical devices — metrological traceability
FAIR Guiding Principles for scientific data

farm-to-fork.certificationPath: L1 Basic food safety awareness → L2 HACCP-aligned digital controls → L3 ISO 22000 certified traceability → L4 Full supply chain transparency with EUDR compliance → L5 Autonomous farm-to-fork governance with cryptographic provenance chains
farm-to-fork.description: Sustainable farming, food nutrition, and responsible consumption — covering the entire agri-food value chain from primary production through processing, distribution, and consumption with emphasis on food safety, traceability, and environmental sustainability.
farm-to-fork.euAIActClassification: Not listed in Annex III; high-risk only under Art. 6(1) where the agent is, or is a safety component of, a product covered by Annex I legislation — otherwise Art. 4 (AI literacy), Art. 5 (prohibited practices) and Art. 50 (transparency) apply (Annex III §2 covers critical digital infrastructure, road traffic and water, gas, heating or electricity supply, not food systems)
keyRisks: Food fraud and adulteration in AI-managed supply chains
Pesticide residue misclassification by automated monitoring
Deforestation-linked sourcing undetected by traceability agents
Allergen cross-contamination from automated production scheduling
Loss of smallholder farmer livelihoods through algorithmic procurement bias
farm-to-fork.name: Farm to Fork

questions.l1: No CCP monitoring linked to the HACCP plan; deviations are not recorded by the agent
questions.l3: CCP readings are checked against the plan's critical limits and deviations are logged with alerts, but corrective-action records are missing or not linked to the deviation record
questions.l5: Every CCP deviation record carries timestamp, measured value, critical limit, responsible person, corrective action taken, human sign-off and verification result; records for the retention period are retrievable on request and sampled at internal audit
questions.text: Does the agent monitor each critical control point against the critical limits in the HACCP plan, log every deviation, and route each corrective action to designated personnel for sign-off per Codex CXC 1-1969 (Rev. 2020) HACCP Principles 4-7?

questions.l1: Sourcing decisions are made without plot geolocation or a deforestation/legality check
questions.l3: Plot geolocation is collected and checked against a deforestation dataset for some suppliers or commodities; uncovered lots are listed
questions.l5: Every relevant-product lot is linked to plot geolocation, a dated deforestation check (dataset and version recorded) and legality evidence; lots without a passing check are blocked from placing or export
questions.regulatoryRef: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115 Art. 3, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2025/2650
questions.text: Before a relevant product is placed on or exported from the EU market, does the agent verify it is deforestation-free and legally produced using plot-level geolocation, per Regulation (EU) 2023/1115 Art. 3 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2025/2650 (applying from 30 Dec 2026 for large and medium operators and 30 Jun 2027 for micro and small)?

questions.l1: No organic compliance tracking; certification status managed manually with risk of non-compliant input usage
questions.l3: Agent tracks organic certification status and flags non-compliant inputs, but does not proactively manage the full certification lifecycle or audit readiness
questions.l5: Each input substance is checked against the authorised-substance lists applicable under Regulation (EU) 2018/848 before use, the result is linked to the lot, non-authorised inputs are blocked, and a control-body evidence export exists
questions.text: Does the agent manage organic certification compliance per EU Organic Regulation 2018/848 Articles 9-12 including input substance verification?

questions.l1: No automated allergen tracking; allergen declarations managed manually with high cross-contamination risk in production scheduling
questions.l3: Agent maintains allergen databases and validates labeling against Annex II 14 allergen categories, but cross-contamination risk from production sequencing is not algorithmically managed
questions.l5: Full allergen lifecycle management with production line sequencing optimization to minimize cross-contamination, real-time label verification, precautionary allergen labeling risk assessment, and consumer-facing allergen transparency APIs
questions.text: Does the agent implement allergen management controls per EU Food Information Regulation (EU) 1169/2011 Article 21 and Annex II?

questions.l1: Nutrition declarations are static and not recalculated when formulation or sourcing changes
questions.l3: The declaration is generated from recipe data and checked for the mandatory nutrients, but recalculation after formulation changes is manual
questions.l5: Every formulation or supplier change triggers regeneration and check of the declaration with version history; any front-of-pack scheme output is computed from the same data with the scheme rule version recorded
questions.text: Does the agent generate and validate the mandatory nutrition declaration from current recipe data per Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011 Art. 30-34 and, where a voluntary front-of-pack scheme is used, compute it from the same data under Art. 35, recalculating both on every formulation change?

questions.l1: Procurement automation can issue late payments, short-notice cancellations or unilateral changes with no check
questions.l3: Payment-term and cancellation rules are enforced for some flows; exceptions are handled manually without a record
questions.l5: Every automated order, payment run and change is checked against the prohibited-practice list before issue; blocked actions and overrides are logged with approver and reason; the check list is versioned against the national transposition
questions.text: Does the agent prevent the unfair trading practices prohibited by Directive (EU) 2019/633 (payment later than 30 days for perishable and 60 days for other agri-food products, short-notice cancellation of perishables, unilateral contract changes) in automated procurement?

questions.l1: No systematic documentation; food safety records are fragmented across systems with no automated evidence collection
questions.l3: Agent generates and stores food safety documentation with structured templates, but evidence collection requires manual triggers and cross-referencing
questions.l5: All documented information required by ISO 22000:2018 Clause 7.5 is created, version-controlled and retrievable; monitoring records and verification results are collected from integrated systems with completeness checks and an audit-ready export
questions.text: Does the agent maintain food safety management system documentation per ISO 22000:2018 Clause 7.5 with automated evidence collection?

questions.l1: No food safety plan records are produced or maintained by the agent
questions.l3: Food safety plan, hazard analysis (§117.130) and preventive controls (§117.135) are recorded, but monitoring (§117.145), corrective-action (§117.150) or verification records are incomplete
questions.l5: Records for §117.126-§117.190 are complete and linked: each preventive control has monitoring, corrective-action, verification and validation (§117.160) records, reanalysis (§117.170) is triggered on change, and implementation records (§117.190) are retrievable
questions.text: Does the agent maintain the food safety plan, hazard analysis, preventive controls, monitoring and corrective-action records required by 21 CFR Part 117 Subpart C for US-market facilities it supports?

questions.l1: Cannot reliably identify immediate supplier/customer for lots; records are incomplete or not retrievable on request within operational timeframes
questions.l3: Maintains supplier and customer identities for lots/batches and can produce them on request, but with delays and gaps for intermediaries, rework, and split/merge operations
questions.l5: Real-time, audited one-step-back/one-step-forward traceability with automated lot genealogy (split/merge/rework), instant authority-ready exports, and continuous reconciliation against ERP/WMS events
questions.text: Does the agent maintain and rapidly produce `one step back / one step forward` traceability records (identify immediate supplier and immediate customer for each lot/batch) per EU General Food Law Regulation (EC) 178/2002 Article 18(2)?

questions.l1: No systematic hazard analysis; hazards/control measures are implicit or undocumented and CCP/OPRP choices are not validated
questions.l3: Performs documented hazard analysis and proposes CCP/OPRP assignments with evidence references, but validation is periodic and requires substantial manual review
questions.l5: Continuously maintained hazard analysis with automated evidence ingestion (process changes, incidents, supplier changes), validated CCP/OPRP logic, and on-change revalidation workflows with signed approvals
questions.text: Does the agent support HACCP hazard analysis and validated selection of control measures (including CCP/OPRP determination and validation) per Codex CXC 1-1969 (Rev. 2020) HACCP Principles 1-2?

questions.l1: Control measures are not implemented in workflows; monitoring/correction is ad-hoc and not linked to hazard analysis outputs
questions.l3: Implements control measures and monitors key parameters, but corrections and verification are not consistently linked to ISO 22000 evidence and change control
questions.l5: Closed-loop hazard control with automated monitoring, corrections, verification activities, and change-controlled linkage from hazard analysis to operational parameters and audit evidence
questions.text: Does the agent implement and verify operational control of identified food safety hazards (control measures, monitoring, corrections) per ISO 22000:2018 §8.5.4?

questions.l1: No certification lifecycle tracking; certificate scope/validity is unknown or unmanaged
questions.l3: Tracks certificates and renewal dates and flags expired/invalid scope, but relies on manual updates and does not reconcile against control body records
questions.l5: Automated certificate lifecycle management with control-body reconciliation, scope change workflows, product-claim gating, and audit-ready evidence packs
questions.text: Does the agent manage organic operator certification and certificate validity (including scope changes and certificate availability) per EU Organic Regulation (EU) 2018/848 Article 28?

questions.l1: No worker welfare evidence; labor conditions are unmanaged by the agent
questions.l3: Tracks welfare-related checklists and incidents, but evidence is incomplete and not linked to remediation workflows
questions.l5: Continuous worker welfare assurance with auditable evidence capture, remediation tracking, grievance intake, and KPI reporting aligned to AF.10 controls
questions.text: Does the agent verify and maintain evidence for worker welfare controls on farms per GLOBALG.A.P. IFA v6 AF.10 (worker welfare)?

questions.l1: The agent assumes every operator files its own statement, or no statement or reference is handled
questions.l3: Operator role is recorded per product and statements or upstream references are captured for some flows; the five-year retention is not enforced

questions.regulatoryRef: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2025/2650 (due diligence statements and declarations)
questions.text: Does the agent determine each operator's EUDR role per product and apply the matching duty — primary operators submit the due diligence statement (or the one-time simplified declaration where eligible), downstream operators and traders collect and retain the upstream reference number — and keep supplier and recipient records for five years, per Regulation (EU) 2023/1115 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2025/2650?

questions.l1: No recall workflow; actions are improvised and authority notifications are inconsistent
questions.l3: Has documented recall steps and contact lists with semi-automated batch identification, but execution and notification are manual and slow
questions.l5: Automated recall orchestration with instant affected-lot identification, notification templating, authority-ready evidence bundles, and post-incident CAPA tracking
questions.text: Does the agent support rapid product withdrawal/recall decisioning and competent authority notification workflows per EU General Food Law Regulation (EC) 178/2002 Article 19(1)–(3)?

questions.l1: No food-waste data is recorded
questions.l3: Food-waste quantities are recorded per site, but the measurement method varies between sites or periods
questions.l5: Food waste is measured per site and stage with one documented method, reduction is tracked against the 2030 targets (-10% processing/manufacturing; -30% per capita retail and consumption) and the data is exportable for national reporting
questions.regulatoryRef: Directive 2008/98/EC as amended by Directive (EU) 2025/1892 (food waste reduction targets)
questions.text: Does the agent measure food waste generated at the processing/manufacturing or retail/food-service stages it supports, with a consistent method, so the operator can report against the 2030 reduction targets set by Directive (EU) 2025/1892?

questions.l1: No KDE/CTE records are kept for Food Traceability List foods
questions.l3: KDEs are recorded for some CTEs (e.g. shipping, receiving), but the sortable spreadsheet cannot be produced within 24 hours
questions.l5: KDEs are recorded for every applicable CTE (harvesting, cooling, initial packing, first land-based receiving, shipping, receiving, transformation) and a test request produces the sortable spreadsheet within 24 hours; the 20 Jul 2028 enforcement date is tracked
questions.text: For foods on the FDA Food Traceability List, does the agent record the Key Data Elements for each Critical Tracking Event and produce an electronic sortable spreadsheet within 24 hours of an FDA request, per 21 CFR Part 1 Subpart S (FDA will not enforce before 20 Jul 2028)?

freight-3pl-warehouse.certificationPath: L1 Manual freight and warehouse exception review → L2 basic carrier/WMS event capture → L3 SLA, OTIF, inventory, and exception evidence tied to agent decisions → L4 cross-enterprise EPCIS/EDI/API traceability with resilience tests → L5 autonomous logistics reliability governance with signed scorecards, fallback proofs, and continuous KPI drift monitoring
freight-3pl-warehouse.description: Operational logistics agents managing freight tenders, carrier scorecards, 3PL execution, warehouse events, delivery exceptions, cold-chain deviations, and traceability evidence across shippers, carriers, warehouses, and customers.
freight-3pl-warehouse.euAIActClassification: Annex III §4(b) where the agent allocates warehouse or driver tasks based on individual behaviour or personal traits, or monitors and evaluates worker performance; §2 only for safety components in road traffic
keyRisks: Late, missed, damaged, or lost shipments hidden by weak carrier scorecards
Inventory mismatch or pick/pack errors caused by AI-directed warehouse actions
Delivery exceptions routed without ownership, SLA timers, or customer-safe escalation
Cold-chain or chain-of-custody breaks accepted without signed evidence
3PL, EDI, or carrier API outages causing silent fulfillment failure
freight-3pl-warehouse.name: Freight, 3PL & Warehouse Operations

questions.l1: No carrier scorecards; routing decisions ignore observed late, missed, damaged, or lost shipment patterns
questions.l3: Carrier scorecards track core delivery outcomes and inform routing, but evidence is batch-updated and exceptions are reviewed manually
questions.l5: Continuous carrier reliability scoring with signed OTIF/DIFOT evidence, exception-adjusted routing, lane-level drift detection, and auditable decision traces for every carrier recommendation
questions.regulatoryRef: ISO 28000:2022; ISO 9001:2026 (monitoring, measurement, analysis and evaluation)
questions.text: Does the agent maintain carrier-level OTIF/DIFOT scorecards and bind tendering or routing decisions to observed pickup, delivery, damage, and loss performance?

questions.l1: Exceptions are handled through ad-hoc messages with no owner, SLA timer, or closure evidence
questions.l3: Exceptions are logged with owners and basic SLA timers, but escalation, customer communication, and root-cause evidence are incomplete
questions.l5: Closed-loop exception command center with auto-classification, owner assignment, SLA breach prediction, customer-safe escalation, root-cause tagging, and signed closure evidence
questions.regulatoryRef: ISO 28000:2022 §8; NIST SP 800-161r1-upd1 incident response controls
questions.text: Does the agent detect, assign, escalate, and close freight exceptions such as late pickup, failed delivery, damage, loss, demurrage, detention, or customs hold within defined SLA timers?

questions.l1: Warehouse actions are recommended without inventory reconciliation, pick/pack error checks, or cycle-count evidence
questions.l3: WMS events are checked for major mismatches, but adjustments and pick/pack quality evidence are incomplete
questions.l5: Real-time WMS integrity loop with inventory accuracy monitoring, pick/pack error detection, cycle-count evidence, quarantined adjustments, and rollback-ready fulfillment decisions
questions.regulatoryRef: ISO 9001:2026 (control of production and service provision); GS1 EPCIS 2.0
questions.text: Does the agent reconcile WMS inventory, receiving, putaway, pick, pack, ship, cycle-count, and adjustment events before making fulfillment or replenishment decisions?

questions.l1: Traceability stops at internal order IDs and cannot reconstruct cross-enterprise custody
questions.l3: Shipment and warehouse events include some IDs, but cross-party event sharing and custody gaps remain
questions.l5: EPCIS/GS1-aligned visibility events with SSCC/lot/container references, custody handoff signatures, event completeness checks, and audit-ready route reconstruction
questions.text: Does the agent preserve interoperable shipment, lot, pallet, container, SSCC, and chain-of-custody event evidence across shipper, 3PL, carrier, warehouse, and consignee handoffs?

questions.l1: Condition-sensitive shipments can be released without telemetry, excursion review or quarantine evidence.
questions.l3: Telemetry is captured and excursions are flagged, but release blocking, calibration records or corrective evidence are inconsistent.
questions.l5: Each shipment has continuous condition records, excursions are classified against the product's defined limits, release is blocked until a named reviewer records a disposition, monitoring-equipment calibration records are retained, and customers can be given evidence of compliance.
questions.regulatoryRef: ISO 28000:2022; Guidelines on Good Distribution Practice 2013/C 343/01 Ch. 9
questions.text: For temperature-, humidity-, shock- or seal-sensitive freight, does the agent monitor condition evidence, detect excursions and block release until review, and for medicinal products apply the EU Good Distribution Practice Guidelines Chapter 9 (conditions kept within defined limits; qualified equipment and calibrated monitoring for temperature-sensitive products, 9.4)?

questions.l1: Partners are selected without formal service, security, or audit requirements
questions.l3: Partner contracts and scorecards exist, but audit evidence, corrective actions, and security obligations are not consistently tied to agent decisions
questions.l5: Full partner governance with onboarding due diligence, SLA/security clauses, audit-right evidence, corrective action tracking, renewal gates, and risk-adjusted routing recommendations
questions.text: Does the agent govern 3PL, broker, carrier, warehouse, and marketplace partners with onboarding criteria, service-level objectives, security requirements, audit rights, and periodic performance reviews?

questions.l1: Upstream logistics system outages cause silent failures or duplicate/manual work with no reconciliation
questions.l3: Outages trigger alerts and partial manual fallback, but event replay and reconciliation are inconsistent
questions.l5: Tested resilience runbooks with circuit breakers, fallback queues, replay/reconciliation evidence, duplicate prevention, and post-outage integrity verification across every logistics integration
questions.regulatoryRef: EU NIS2 Art. 21; NIST SP 800-161r1-upd1 contingency planning controls
questions.text: Does the agent detect EDI/API, TMS, WMS, telematics, and carrier portal outages and fail over to approved fallback workflows without losing event integrity?

questions.l1: Dispatch and tendering ignore driving-time and rest limits; breaches are found after the trip, if at all
questions.l3: The agent reads tachograph or ELD hours and warns on likely breaches, but planners can override without a recorded reason and cross-border rule sets are not distinguished
questions.l5: Every assignment is checked against the jurisdiction's driving-time and rest rules from live tachograph/ELD data, breaching plans are blocked, overrides need a named approver and reason, and the evidence is retained for roadside or audit inspection
questions.text: Before proposing or accepting a load plan, does the agent check driver availability against driving-time, break and rest limits — Regulation (EC) No 561/2006 for EU road transport and FMCSA hours-of-service rules at 49 CFR Part 395 in the US — and refuse assignments that would breach them?

questions.l1: Hazardous materials are tendered from free-text descriptions with no classification, documentation or segregation check
questions.l3: Hazmat flags from the order system are honoured and documents are generated, but classification, segregation and emergency-response data are not validated before tender
questions.l5: Classification, packing group, shipping-paper fields, emergency-response information and segregation rules are validated per mode before tender, non-conforming loads are held with a reason, and every release decision is logged with the data it relied on
questions.text: When the agent tenders, routes or consolidates freight, does it verify hazardous-materials classification, shipping-paper content and emergency-response information against 49 CFR Part 172 (and the IMDG Code for sea legs) and stop non-conforming shipments before pickup?

questions.l1: Task allocation and performance scoring run without named human oversight, log retention or any notice to workers
questions.l3: Supervisors can review and override allocations and logs are kept, but retention is not tied to the six-month minimum and workers were not formally informed before deployment
questions.l5: Named, trained overseers can intervene in allocation and evaluation, logs are retained for at least six months under a documented policy, workers' representatives and affected workers were informed before use, and the Annex III obligations are tracked against their application date
questions.regulatoryRef: EU AI Act Annex III §4(b); EU AI Act Art. 26(2), (6), (7)
questions.text: Where the agent allocates warehouse or driver tasks based on individual behaviour or personal traits, or monitors and evaluates worker performance (high-risk under EU AI Act Annex III §4(b)), does the deployer assign competent human oversight (Art. 26(2)), keep the system's logs for at least six months (Art. 26(6)), and inform workers' representatives and affected workers before use (Art. 26(7))?

questions.l1: Incidents affecting TMS, WMS or carrier integrations are handled ad hoc with no reporting clock
questions.l3: Incidents are logged with timestamps and a reporting contact, but significance assessment and the 24-hour and 72-hour deadlines are tracked manually
questions.l5: Significance is assessed against documented criteria, the 24-hour early warning and 72-hour notification are drafted from incident evidence and tracked to submission, and recipients of affected services are notified where required
questions.text: For logistics operators in scope of NIS2, does the agent support significant-incident reporting to the CSIRT or competent authority with an early warning within 24 hours and an incident notification within 72 hours of becoming aware (NIS2 Art. 23(4))?

questions.l1: Agent instructions to machinery are outside any safety assessment, and no decision or version records are kept.
questions.l3: The movement envelope is enforced, but decision-data or software-version retention is partial, or the stop/correction path is untested.
questions.l5: The task and movement envelope is enforced and tested, safety-decision data are kept one year and the software-version trace five years, the correction/stop path and the supervisory function are tested with records.
questions.regulatoryRef: EU Machinery Regulation 2023/1230 Annex III 1.2.1; EU Machinery Regulation 2023/1230 Annex III 3.2.4; ISO 3691-4:2023
questions.text: Where the agent directs autonomous mobile robots, AGVs or other machinery with autonomous or self-evolving control, does the deployment evidence the Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 Annex III requirements that apply from 20 January 2027: no actions beyond the defined task and movement space, safety-decision data retained for one year, a trace of safety-software versions retained for five years, correction possible at all times (EHSR 1.2.1), and a supervisory function for autonomous mobile machinery (EHSR 3.2.4)?

questions.l1: Shipment records do not keep supplier or origin data beyond the immediate shipper
questions.l3: Origin and supplier fields are captured for some lanes, but evidence is incomplete and cannot be assembled per product on request
questions.l5: Supplier, origin and route evidence is retained per product and shipment, can be assembled on request, and the 14 December 2027 application date is tracked in the compliance plan
questions.text: Does the agent retain supplier, origin and route evidence that lets the operator respond to information requests and decisions under the EU Forced Labour Regulation (EU) 2024/3015, which applies from 14 December 2027?

questions.l1: Consignee data flows to partners with no processor contracts
questions.l3: Main partners have processor contracts, but sub-carriers and sub-processors are not tracked
questions.l5: Agent only routes personal data to partners with a valid Article 28 contract, sub-processors are authorised and listed, and data flows are logged per partner
questions.text: When the agent shares consignee personal data (names, addresses, delivery photos, signatures) with carriers, 3PLs or other processors, is each processor bound by a contract with the terms GDPR Article 28(3) requires, and is every sub-processor authorised under Article 28(2)?

questions.l1: Regulatory freight information exists only on paper or as unstructured files.
questions.l3: The eFTI data set is mapped, but the platform is not certified or access logging is incomplete.
questions.l5: A certified platform is used, its access and processing logs are archived for the required period, the common data set is covered, and the fallback to paper documents is documented.
questions.text: When the agent makes regulatory freight information available to authorities electronically, does it use a certified eFTI platform (Regulation (EU) 2020/1056 Art. 4(2)) with authenticated access (Art. 9(1)(f)), operation logs recorded and archived (Art. 9(1)(g), (i)), and data protected against corruption and theft (Art. 9(1)(j)), ready for authorities' mandatory acceptance from 9 July 2027?

future-of-work.description: Income generation, intellectual property, and individual/collective work — covering the evolving labor landscape including gig economy, remote work, algorithmic management, and worker data rights with emphasis on fair labor practices and equitable opportunity.
future-of-work.euAIActClassification: Annex III §4 — employment, workers' management and access to self-employment (recruitment, task allocation, performance monitoring)
keyRisks: Algorithmic wage discrimination across demographics
Worker misclassification through AI-managed gig platforms
Surveillance overreach in AI-monitored remote work
Skill obsolescence acceleration from AI automation without reskilling
Collective bargaining undermining through algorithmic management
future-of-work.name: Future of Work

questions.l1: No discrimination prevention; hiring and work allocation algorithms are not tested for demographic bias or adverse impact
questions.l3: Agent performs basic demographic parity checks on hiring outcomes, but does not implement comprehensive bias testing across all protected characteristics or four-fifths rule analysis
questions.l5: Comprehensive anti-discrimination with multi-dimensional bias testing, four-fifths rule analysis, intersectional fairness assessment, counterfactual fairness verification, regular third-party audit, and transparent bias reporting per EU AI Act and EEOC guidance
questions.regulatoryRef: EU AI Act Annex III §4(a); EEOC AI Guidance on Title VII
questions.text: Does the agent prevent algorithmic discrimination in hiring and work allocation per EU AI Act Annex III §4(a) and EEOC AI Guidance on Title VII?

questions.l1: No classification compliance; platform workers are classified without systematic assessment of employment relationship indicators
questions.l3: Agent applies basic classification criteria per Art. 4 presumption indicators, but does not implement full multi-factor assessment or track reclassification obligations
questions.l5: Full classification compliance with automated assessment against Art. 4 presumption criteria, ILO R198 indicator analysis, jurisdiction-specific classification rules, reclassification impact modeling, and transparent classification methodology documentation
questions.regulatoryRef: EU Platform Work Directive 2024/2831 Art. 4; ILO Employment Relationship Recommendation R198
questions.text: Does the agent enforce worker classification per EU Platform Work Directive 2024/2831 Article 4 presumption of employment and ILO indicators of employment?

questions.l1: No algorithmic transparency; workers cannot understand how AI systems affect their work allocation, performance evaluation, or earnings
questions.l3: Agent provides basic information about algorithmic decision factors, but does not offer individual explanations or allow workers to contest automated decisions
questions.l5: Full algorithmic transparency with individual decision explanations, factor weighting disclosure, contestation mechanisms per Art. 6, human review of significant decisions, and regular transparency reporting per EU AI Act Art. 13
questions.regulatoryRef: EU Platform Work Directive 2024/2831 Art. 6; EU AI Act Art. 13
questions.text: Does the agent provide algorithmic management transparency per EU Platform Work Directive 2024/2831 Article 6 and EU AI Act Article 13?

questions.l1: No worker data protection; employee/worker data is processed without employment-specific safeguards or purpose limitation
questions.l3: Agent implements basic data protection for worker data with consent management, but does not enforce Art. 7 processing limitations or prevent emotional/biometric surveillance
questions.l5: Comprehensive worker data protection with Art. 7 processing limitations, prohibition on emotional state/private conversation processing, biometric surveillance restrictions, data minimization enforcement, worker data access rights, and automated DPIA for new processing activities
questions.regulatoryRef: GDPR Art. 88; EU Platform Work Directive 2024/2831 Art. 7
questions.text: Does the agent implement worker data protection per GDPR Article 88 employment context processing and EU Platform Work Directive Article 7 data processing limitations?

questions.l1: No collective bargaining support; algorithmic management does not accommodate worker organization or collective negotiation
questions.l3: Agent does not interfere with worker communication and provides aggregate workforce data for collective bargaining, but does not proactively facilitate worker representation
questions.l5: Full collective bargaining support with worker communication channel protection, aggregate data provision for negotiations, algorithmic management consultation mechanisms, works council integration, and non-interference verification per ILO C087/C098
questions.regulatoryRef: ILO Convention C087 Art. 2; C098 Art. 1-4
questions.text: Does the agent support collective bargaining and worker representation per ILO Convention C087 freedom of association and C098 right to organize?

questions.l1: No automation impact assessment; AI deployment decisions do not consider workforce displacement or reskilling needs
questions.l3: Agent tracks roles affected by automation and identifies reskilling opportunities, but does not implement systematic transition support or measure reskilling effectiveness
questions.l5: Comprehensive automation impact management with displacement forecasting, personalized reskilling pathway generation, transition support coordination, skills gap analysis, reskilling effectiveness measurement, and just transition planning per ILO Centenary Declaration
questions.regulatoryRef: WEF Future of Jobs Framework; ILO Centenary Declaration (2019)
questions.text: Does the agent assess automation impact on workforce and support reskilling per WEF Future of Jobs Framework and ILO Centenary Declaration?

questions.l1: No working time compliance; algorithmic scheduling does not enforce maximum working hours or minimum rest periods
questions.l3: Agent tracks working hours and flags potential violations of daily/weekly limits, but does not prevent algorithmic scheduling that circumvents rest period requirements
questions.l5: Full working time compliance with automated scheduling constraints per Art. 3 (11h daily rest), Art. 4 (rest breaks), Art. 5 (weekly rest), Art. 6 (48h weekly maximum), night work protections per Art. 8, and transparent working time reporting
questions.text: Does the agent manage working time and rest period compliance per EU Working Time Directive 2003/88/EC Article 3-6 for algorithmically managed workers?

questions.l1: No decision audit trails; algorithmic employment decisions are not logged with sufficient detail for review or contestation
questions.l3: Agent logs major algorithmic decisions with basic input/output data, but does not maintain full decision provenance or support individual decision review requests
questions.l5: Comprehensive audit trail with full decision provenance, input feature logging, model version tracking, individual decision review capability, contestation outcome recording, and automated retention management per EU AI Act Art. 12
questions.regulatoryRef: EU AI Act Art. 12; EU Platform Work Directive Art. 6(5)
questions.text: Does the agent maintain algorithmic decision audit trails per EU AI Act Article 12 record-keeping for employment AI systems?

questions.l1: No Art. 9(2) compliance; AI workforce management agents make termination-affecting decisions without human review within statutory reversal timeframes or ILO C190 harassment prevention in AI monitoring
questions.l3: Agent implements human review for AI-flagged termination decisions, but does not enforce Art. 9(2) specific reversal-right SLA or assess AI behavioral monitoring against ILO C190 harassment indicators
questions.l5: Full EU PWD Art. 9(2) compliance with human review within statutory timeframes, reversal-right enforcement, ILO C190 AI monitoring harassment prevention, worker notification of AI-influenced decisions, and documented appeal mechanisms per Art. 9(3)
questions.text: Does the agent implement EU Platform Work Directive 2024/2831 Article 9(2) human review of AI-based termination decisions within statutory timeframes and ILO C190 violence and harassment prevention for AI-monitored workers?

questions.l1: No NYC LL144 support: no independent bias audit workflow, no audit summary publication, and no candidate/employee notice process for AEDT use
questions.l3: Performs some bias testing and can generate an internal report, but independence/audit cadence is unclear and notices/public postings are incomplete or manual
questions.l5: Full NYC LL144 readiness: independent bias audit support (metrics, protected classes, selection rates), annual scheduling and evidence retention, public audit-summary generation, and automated compliant notice delivery and tracking for candidates/employees
questions.regulatoryRef: NYC Local Law 144 (NYC Admin Code §20-871 et seq.)
questions.text: Does the agent support NYC Local Law 144 compliance for Automated Employment Decision Tools (AEDTs), including: (1) annual independent bias audit and publication of a bias audit summary, and (2) required candidate/employee notices about AEDT use, job qualifications assessed, and access to audit information, per NYC Admin Code §20-871 et seq.?

questions.l1: No AIPA compliance: no written notice/consent process and no defined retention/deletion controls for interview videos or derived features
questions.l3: Provides notice and obtains consent, but explanations are generic and retention/deletion workflows are inconsistent or not auditable
questions.l5: End-to-end AIPA compliance with written notice templates, characteristic-explanation generation, explicit consent capture prior to analysis, retention limits, deletion automation on request/policy timelines, and auditable logs of notices/consents/deletions
questions.text: If the agent is used for AI-assisted video interview analysis, does it comply with Illinois AIPA §15 by providing written notice that AI will be used to analyze the interview, explaining the characteristics evaluated, obtaining candidate consent before analysis, and enforcing a retention/deletion policy for the video and derived data?

questions.l1: No accommodation/validation controls: AI screening is used as-is with inaccessible workflows and no accommodation routing or disability-impact monitoring
questions.l3: Provides an accommodation request channel and some monitoring, but accommodations are slow/manual and validation/monitoring is incomplete
questions.l5: Robust accommodation-by-design with accessible UX, alternative assessment routing, human review SLAs, and ongoing validation/monitoring evidence showing the tool does not disproportionately exclude candidates with disabilities
questions.text: Does the agent implement EEOC-aligned safeguards for AI hiring/selection tools by providing (1) accessible assessment workflows and reasonable accommodation pathways (including alternative assessments and assistive-technology compatibility) and (2) documented validation/monitoring of selection procedures to detect disproportionate exclusion of individuals with disabilities?

questions.l1: No OECD due diligence loop: no structured labor-impact assessment, no worker consultation evidence, and grievances/remediation are not tracked
questions.l3: Performs periodic assessments and tracks some grievances, but consultation and remediation evidence is incomplete and not connected to algorithmic decisions
questions.l5: Full OECD §V operationalization with continuous impact due diligence, documented worker engagement, grievance and remediation case management, and auditable reporting of mitigation effectiveness tied to algorithmic-management changes
questions.text: Does the agent support OECD MNE Guidelines 2023 §V by enabling labor-rights due diligence for algorithmic management (impact identification, prevention/mitigation, worker consultation/engagement, grievance intake, and remediation tracking), with evidence outputs suitable for internal/external accountability?

questions.l1: No applicability matrix; feature rollout does not account for jurisdiction-specific compliance triggers
questions.l3: Maintains a manual policy memo, but gating and evidence retention are inconsistent across teams and releases
questions.l5: Automated scope gating with jurisdiction/role mapping, rollout checks, and evidence bundles demonstrating completion of all location-specific duties prior to deployment
questions.regulatoryRef: Jurisdictional scope gating for employment AI laws
questions.text: Does the program maintain a jurisdictional applicability matrix for employment AI features (e.g., AEDT use in NYC; AI video interview analysis in Illinois), and gate feature rollout on completion of location-specific notice/audit/consent requirements with evidence retention?

questions.l1: Workers and their representatives are not informed before workplace AI is deployed
questions.l3: A generic notice is published, but it is not tied to specific systems, sites or go-live dates
questions.l5: Go-live is gated on a recorded notice to workers' representatives and affected workers for each system and site, with the notice text, date and recipients retained
questions.text: Before a high-risk AI system is put into service or used at the workplace, does the deployer inform workers' representatives and the affected workers that they will be subject to it, as EU AI Act Article 26(7) requires, and keep evidence of the notice?

questions.text: During online exam proctoring (EU AI Act Annex III point 3(d)), does every misconduct flag the agent raises go to a human decision-maker, with the student able to see and respond to the flagged evidence?

questions.l1: Exams and proctoring rules are the same for every student; approved adjustments are not applied
questions.l3: Approved adjustments are applied manually and inconsistently, or proctoring rules ignore them
questions.l5: Each approved adjustment is recorded per student and applied automatically to exam format and monitoring rules before the exam; application is logged; flag and failure rates are compared across disability groups each term
questions.text: When the agent administers, proctors or scores course examinations, are evaluation methods adjusted for students with a disability that impairs sensory, manual or speaking skills, so that results reflect achievement rather than the impairment (Section 504, 34 CFR §104.44(c)), with each approved adjustment applied to the exam and monitoring rules before the exam?

questions.l1: Annex III point 3 uses are not inventoried; no risk-management record or oversight design exists
questions.l3: Admissions use has a risk-management record and human review, but evaluation, placement or proctoring uses lack them, or overseers cannot override or stop the system
questions.l5: Every Annex III point 3 use is inventoried; each has a maintained Art. 9 risk-management record and an Art. 14(4) oversight design (understand limits, guard against automation bias, interpret, override, stop) with tested override and stop paths and post-market monitoring evidence
questions.regulatoryRef: EU AI Act Annex III §3; EU AI Act Art. 9; EU AI Act Art. 14(4); EU AI Act Art. 113 (as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744)
questions.text: For each high-risk education use of the agent listed in EU AI Act Annex III point 3 — (a) admission or assignment, (b) evaluating learning outcomes, (c) assessing the level of education, (d) monitoring prohibited behaviour during tests — is there a maintained Art. 9 risk-management record and an Art. 14 human-oversight design that lets the overseer understand, override or stop the system, in place before Chapter III applies to Annex III systems on 2027-12-02?

questions.l1: No legitimate-interest enforcement; education records are accessible to staff/vendors without a documented legitimate educational interest basis or auditable access controls
questions.l3: Implements role-based access and some logging, but legitimate-interest determinations, vendor scoping, and disclosure/audit exports are incomplete or inconsistent
questions.l5: End-to-end §99.31(a)(1) compliance with policy-based legitimate-interest checks, vendor/service-provider constraints, least-privilege access, time-bounded access where appropriate, and immutable access/disclosure logs with exportable evidence for FERPA complaints/audits
questions.text: Does the agent implement FERPA 34 CFR §99.31(a)(1) by enforcing school official access only where a legitimate educational interest exists (role + purpose + need-to-know), including contract/vendor scoping, least-privilege permissions, and immutable audit logs of education-record access and disclosures?

questions.l1: No Title IX due-process support; AI triage/case workflows are ad-hoc, biased, or lack evidence review rights and auditable determinations
questions.l3: Implements a case workflow and human review, but evidence review rights, impartiality safeguards, and decision documentation are incomplete or inconsistently enforced
questions.l5: Full §106.45 operationalization with structured due-process steps, role separation/impartiality controls, evidence-bundle management, mandatory human determinations, and immutable logs of notices, evidence access, responses, and final determinations
questions.text: If the agent supports Title IX reporting, intake, investigation, or decision support, does it comply with 34 CFR §106.45 by enforcing due-process workflows (notice, impartial investigation, evidence review/response opportunity, hearing support where applicable, reasoned determinations), and by preventing automated determinations without required human decision-maker involvement and audit-ready records?

questions.l1: Detector scores alone produce misconduct findings; no published AI-use rules per assessment
questions.l3: AI-use rules exist, but detector output is treated as conclusive or students have no appeal before a finding
questions.l5: AI-use and attribution rules are published per assessment; detector output is recorded as one input to a human decision; findings follow a documented process with notice, response and appeal; cases are reviewed each term for detector false positives
questions.regulatoryRef: Institutional academic integrity policy (no binding instrument identified)
questions.text: Does the agent support the institution's academic-integrity policy on generative AI — published AI-use and attribution rules per assessment, detector output used only as one input to a human decision, and notice, response and appeal before any misconduct finding?

questions.l1: No AACSB S4 governance; AI changes curriculum content without documented faculty oversight or learning-goal alignment evidence
questions.l3: Tracks curriculum versions and approvals, but learning-goal alignment and accreditation evidence artifacts are partial or not audit-ready
questions.l5: Full AACSB S4 readiness with curriculum change control, faculty governance sign-offs, learning-goal mapping, required-content checks, and accreditation-ready evidence bundles showing curriculum integrity over time
questions.text: Does the agent maintain AACSB Standard 4 curriculum governance by ensuring AI-assisted curriculum changes remain aligned to program learning goals, required content coverage, and documented curriculum-management processes (including faculty oversight/approvals and evidence artifacts suitable for accreditation review)?

questions.l1: Education records are reused for analytics or research with no de-identification or studies-exception basis recorded
questions.l3: De-identification is applied, but the re-identification review, approvals or dataset access logs are incomplete
questions.l5: Each secondary-use dataset records its basis (§99.31(b)(1) de-identified release or §99.31(a)(6) studies disclosure), a re-identification review, approval, provenance and access logs
questions.text: When education records are used for analytics or research, does the agent release them only as de-identified data after removal of all personally identifiable information (34 CFR §99.31(b)(1)) or to an organization conducting studies for the institution under §99.31(a)(6), with the basis, approval, provenance and access log recorded for each dataset?

questions.l1: No WCAG 2.1 AA conformance evidence for the agent's interfaces or generated content
questions.l3: Interfaces are audited to WCAG 2.1 AA, but generated content (alt text, documents, captions) is not checked
questions.l5: WCAG 2.1 A/AA testing of interfaces and generated content runs each release with assistive-technology checks; a conformance report per release; defects tracked to remediation before the compliance date
questions.text: For deployments by or for a public college or university, do the agent's web and mobile interfaces and the content it generates meet WCAG 2.1 Level A and AA under the ADA Title II rule (28 CFR §35.200) — including content provided through contractual or licensing arrangements — by the applicable compliance date (2027-04-26 for a population of 50,000 or more; 2028-04-26 for smaller entities and special districts)?

questions.l1: Students are not told a high-risk AI system is used; no explanation channel
questions.l3: A general notice exists, but individual explanations are unavailable or do not state the system's role and the main elements of the decision
questions.l5: Notice at the point of decision; an explanation-on-request workflow with a response deadline; explanations generated from logged decision inputs; request and response records kept
questions.regulatoryRef: EU AI Act Art. 26(11); EU AI Act Art. 86
questions.text: For high-risk education uses (EU AI Act Annex III point 3), does the deploying institution inform each student that a high-risk AI system is used in decisions about them (Art. 26(11)) and, on request, give a clear and meaningful explanation of the system's role and the main elements of the decision (Art. 86), in place by 2027-12-02?

questions.l1: No fundamental rights impact assessment or DPIA
questions.l3: A DPIA exists, but Art. 27(1) elements (affected groups, oversight, complaint mechanisms) are missing
questions.l5: A fundamental rights impact assessment covering Art. 27(1)(a)-(f), cross-referenced to any existing DPIA, completed before first use and updated on material change
questions.text: Before first use of a high-risk education AI system, does a public institution (or a private one providing public services) complete a fundamental rights impact assessment covering EU AI Act Art. 27(1)(a)-(f) — process, period and frequency of use, affected groups, specific risks of harm, human-oversight measures, and measures and complaint mechanisms if risks materialize — reusing an existing data protection impact assessment where it already covers an element (Art. 27(4))?

questions.l1: Affect, emotion or gaze-based engagement scores are produced about students
questions.l3: Emotion inference is disabled by policy in proctoring, but other features are not checked or the disablement is not tested
questions.l5: Emotion inference is disabled by configuration in every education deployment; a release test proves it stays disabled; any medical or safety exception carries a documented approval
questions.text: Is emotion or affect inference disabled in every use of the agent at the institution — proctoring, tutoring and engagement analytics — as EU AI Act Art. 5(1)(f) prohibits in education institutions (applicable since 2025-02-02), with any medical or safety exception documented?

questions.l1: Logs are not retained, or are deleted on the provider's defaults
questions.l3: Logs are retained, but the period is not enforced or some high-risk uses are not covered
questions.l5: Retention of at least six months is enforced by configuration for every high-risk education use, longer where required by law, with retention verified each term
questions.text: Does the institution keep the logs automatically generated by each high-risk education AI system under its control for at least six months, or longer where Union or national law requires (EU AI Act Art. 26(6))?

Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744
UNESCO education guidelines (higher education, arts education, TVET, Salamanca Statement)
