public-private-collaboration.certificationPath: L1 Basic PPP governance → L2 UNCAC anti-corruption controls → L3 OECD/World Bank PPP framework → L4 Full UNGPs human rights due diligence → L5 Autonomous accountability-verified partnership orchestration with SDG impact measurement
public-private-collaboration.description: Connecting public institutions (national/state governments, WHO, UN) and private institutions in growth-oriented transformations — AI agents orchestrating public-private partnerships for sustainable development with accountability, anti-corruption safeguards, and equitable value distribution.
public-private-collaboration.euAIActClassification: Depends on use case; not Annex III point 8. Annex III point 5 applies only where the agent evaluates eligibility for public assistance (5(a)) or similar listed uses; the GPAI systemic-risk designation applies to models, not to this pack's use cases
keyRisks: Corruption facilitation through AI-mediated contract procurement
Value extraction asymmetry benefiting private partners over public interest
Anti-competitive behavior enabled by AI partnership intelligence
Human rights violations in PPP projects without adequate due diligence
AI-enabled revolving door between public regulators and private interests
public-private-collaboration.name: Public and Private Collaboration

questions.l1: No anti-corruption controls; AI-mediated PPP procurement lacks UNCAC-required transparency, conflict of interest disclosure, or competitive tendering safeguards
questions.l3: Agent implements basic procurement transparency and conflict of interest screening, but does not systematically apply UNCAC Art. 7 public sector integrity or Art. 9 procurement controls
questions.l5: Full UNCAC compliance with Art. 7 public sector integrity controls, Art. 9 procurement transparency, beneficial ownership verification, conflict of interest automated screening, bribery risk assessment in PPP activities, and anti-corruption audit trail per UNCAC Chapter IV
questions.text: Does the agent implement anti-corruption controls per UNCAC Articles 7 and 9 requirements for public procurement and financial management transparency in AI-mediated PPP activities?

questions.l1: No human rights due diligence; PPP projects are evaluated without UNGPs §17-21 human rights impact assessment or remediation mechanisms for private partner activities
questions.l3: Agent includes human rights risk indicators in partner assessment, but does not implement full UNGPs §17-21 due diligence cycle or operational grievance mechanisms
questions.l5: Full UNGPs due diligence with §17-21 human rights impact assessment for all PPP private partners, ongoing monitoring, stakeholder engagement with affected communities per §18, grievance mechanism per §29, and transparent human rights reporting
questions.text: Does the agent implement human rights due diligence per UN Guiding Principles §17-21 for private partners in PPP projects with potential adverse human rights impacts?

questions.l1: PPP contract information is not published
questions.l3: Summaries are published, but not as OCDS-conformant data, or amendments and renegotiations are missing
questions.l5: OCDS-conformant releases for every contracting stage including amendments and renegotiations, validated against the schema before publication, with performance data updated on a published schedule
questions.text: Does the agent publish PPP contracting data — tender, award, contract terms, amendments and renegotiations, and performance — as structured open data conforming to the Open Contracting Data Standard 1.1 (latest release 1.1.5), with the PPP extension fields where used?

questions.l1: No ISMS scope covers PPP systems or data
questions.l3: Controls exist for PPP data, but the ISMS scope or certification does not cover the agent, or the AI system's own security was not assessed
questions.l5: ISMS scope includes the agent and PPP data, role-based access to sensitive terms is enforced and reviewed, and an AI-specific security assessment is on file for each release
questions.regulatoryRef: ISO/IEC 27001:2022; OECD AI Principles (robustness, security and safety)
questions.text: Are PPP systems the agent uses, and the partnership and procurement data it handles, covered by an information security management system meeting ISO/IEC 27001:2022, with access to sensitive partnership terms restricted by role and the security of the AI system itself (robustness, security and safety, OECD AI Principles) assessed before deployment?

questions.l1: No fiscal risk management; PPP AI does not assess or monitor contingent liabilities, guarantees, or fiscal exposure from partnership commitments
questions.l3: Agent tracks PPP fiscal commitments and flags budget impacts, but does not implement IMF PFRAM-level fiscal risk quantification or OECD DAC blended finance monitoring
questions.l5: Full fiscal risk governance with IMF PFRAM implementation, contingent liability assessment, guarantee exposure monitoring, OECD DAC blended finance compliance, fiscal risk disclosure per IMF standards, and parliamentary budget office integration for oversight
questions.regulatoryRef: IMF PFRAM; OECD DAC Blended Finance Principles
questions.text: Does the agent implement fiscal risk management per IMF PFRAM (PPP Fiscal Risk Assessment Model) and OECD DAC Blended Finance Guidelines for public finance protection?

questions.l1: No competition compliance; AI-managed PPP activities may involve anti-competitive market allocation, bid rigging, or public procurement manipulation without detection
questions.l3: Agent monitors PPP activities for obvious competition law violations and maintains procurement compliance, but does not implement systematic TFEU Art. 101-102 assessment or AI-enabled collusion detection
questions.l5: Full competition compliance with TFEU Art. 101-102 monitoring, AI-enabled collusion detection in procurement, EU Directive 2014/24 public procurement compliance, competition authority reporting capability, market concentration assessment for PPP portfolios, and antitrust risk assessment for all AI-managed partnership decisions
questions.text: Does the agent implement competition law compliance per EU Treaty on the Functioning of the EU Articles 101-102 and national competition authority requirements for AI-managed PPP market activities?

questions.l1: PPP financial flows and partners are not risk-rated
questions.l3: Partners are rated at onboarding, but individual flows are not rated or ratings are not reviewed on change
questions.l5: Every PPP partner and flow has a documented risk rating, controls scaled to it, and ratings reviewed on each material change with evidence
questions.text: Does the agent apply a risk-based approach to PPP financial flows (FATF Recommendation 1), rating each partner and flow for money-laundering and terrorist-financing risk, scaling controls to the rating, and reviewing ratings on change?

questions.l1: Criteria are not published in advance, evaluation cannot be reproduced, and bidders have no review route
questions.l3: Criteria and some evaluation logs exist, but AI-assisted scoring cannot be reproduced or the review route is not documented
questions.l5: Published criteria before tender, reproducible evaluation records separating AI suggestions from evaluator decisions, published award information, and a documented review and appeal route with case outcomes
questions.text: Does the agent implement UNCAC Art. 9(1)(a)-(d) procurement transparency for PPP procurements by ensuring (1) public distribution of procurement information and award information, (2) conditions for participation and selection and award criteria set and published in advance, (3) objective and predetermined criteria applied with evaluation records that allow later verification, including where AI assisted, and (4) an effective domestic review and appeal route for bidders?

questions.l1: Decisions are made without a pre-test, comparator or risk-allocation analysis
questions.l3: A business case exists, but the comparator, risk allocation or the link from AI recommendations to the rationale is missing
questions.l5: Pre-test, comparator with published methodology, risk-allocation matrix and sensitivity analysis on file per project, with AI recommendations traceable to each element
questions.text: Does the agent support PPP value-for-money decisions as the OECD PPP Recommendation sets out: a procurement option pre-test comparing lifetime costs of finance, construction and operation across delivery modes (Principle 5, Annex 5.1), a public sector comparator with a published methodology where relevant (Annex 5.2), and risk allocated to the party that can manage it at least cost (Principle 6, Annex 6.1), with an evidence bundle linking AI recommendations to the value-for-money rationale?

questions.l1: Anti-bribery controls are ad hoc and not applied to partners or intermediaries
questions.l3: A policy exists and some partners are screened, but intermediary due diligence, reporting channels or records are incomplete
questions.l5: Policy applied to every partner and intermediary, due diligence on file and refreshed on change, a protected reporting channel with case logs, and records of contributions and lobbying contacts
questions.text: Does the agent support an anti-corruption programme across PPP partners and intermediaries — anti-bribery policy, third-party due diligence, gifts and hospitality controls, protected reporting channels, and records of political contributions and lobbying contacts — consistent with ISO 26000 clause 6.6.3 (anti-corruption) and the private-sector measures of UNCAC Art. 12?

questions.l1: AI influence on PPP decisions is not recorded and no official is accountable
questions.l3: Officials are named, but the log does not separate AI suggestions from decisions or rationales are not published
questions.l5: Decision log separating AI suggestion and human decision for every decision, named accountable official, published rationale, and a contest route with logged outcomes
questions.regulatoryRef: OECD AI Principles (accountability); EU AI Act Art. 26
questions.text: For AI-influenced PPP decisions (procurement shortlists, risk-allocation recommendations, renegotiation triggers), does the operator keep a decision log that separates AI suggestions from the final human decision, name the accountable official, publish a rationale suitable for oversight, and offer affected bidders a route to contest, consistent with the accountability principle of the OECD AI Recommendation and, where the system is high-risk, the deployer duties of EU AI Act Art. 26?

questions.l1: Standard vendor terms; agency data may be used to train vendor models
questions.l3: The training prohibition is present, but portability, knowledge-transfer or licensing terms are missing
questions.l5: Contract clause library covering every M-25-22 term, each AI contract checked against it before signature, and an exit plan tested for data and model portability
questions.text: Do contracts with private AI vendors in US federal partnerships include the OMB M-25-22 terms: a permanent prohibition on using non-public agency inputs and outputs to further train publicly or commercially available AI without explicit agency consent, and vendor lock-in protections (knowledge transfer, data and model portability, clear licensing, pricing transparency)?

questions.l1: Public-sector data requests are fulfilled without checks
questions.l3: Requests are reviewed manually without recorded criteria
questions.l5: Structured intake checking each Art. 15 condition, data minimised to the request, return or deletion tracked, and every decision logged
questions.regulatoryRef: EU Data Act Arts 14-15 (Regulation (EU) 2023/2854, applies from 12 Sep 2025)
questions.text: When a private partner receives a public-sector request for data on grounds of exceptional need, does the agent check the request against the Data Act conditions (Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 Arts 14-15: demonstrated exceptional need, purpose, scope and time limits) before data is released, release only what is necessary, and log the decision?

questions.l1: Beneficial owners of partners and special-purpose vehicles are not identified
questions.l3: Beneficial owners are identified at onboarding, but those of special-purpose vehicles are not verified or not re-checked on change, or no AMLR gap plan exists
questions.l5: Beneficial owners of every partner and vehicle are verified and re-checked on change, and an AMLR gap plan with owners is dated before 10 Jul 2027
questions.text: Does the agent verify the beneficial owners of PPP partners and special-purpose vehicles, re-check them on change, and track a gap plan for the EU Anti-Money Laundering Regulation, which applies from 10 Jul 2027 (Regulation (EU) 2024/1624)?

questions.l1: The private partner has not done a fundamental rights impact assessment
questions.l3: An assessment exists, but it omits some Art. 27(1) elements or post-dates first use, or the authority was not notified
questions.l5: An assessment with all Art. 27(1)(a)-(f) elements before first use, the notification recorded, updates recorded when any element changes, and the contract assigning this duty to the partner
questions.regulatoryRef: EU AI Act Art. 27(1), 27(3) (Annex III obligations from 2 Dec 2027)
questions.text: Where a private partner provides a public service through the agent and the agent is an Annex III high-risk system, has the partner, as a private entity providing public services, completed a fundamental rights impact assessment covering EU AI Act Art. 27(1)(a)-(f) before first use and notified its results to the market surveillance authority (Art. 27(3))?

sip-to-sanitation.certificationPath: L1 Basic water quality monitoring → L2 WHO guideline compliance automation → L3 EU WFD good ecological status tracking → L4 Predictive water resource management → L5 Autonomous water ecosystem governance with verified sustainability outcomes
sip-to-sanitation.description: River, ocean, sea, and marine resources — covering water sustainability from source protection through treatment, distribution, consumption, wastewater management, and marine ecosystem preservation.
sip-to-sanitation.euAIActClassification: Annex III §2 — safety components in the management and operation of the supply of water
keyRisks: Drinking water contamination from AI-managed treatment process failures
Marine ecosystem damage from undetected wastewater discharge violations
Water scarcity exacerbation through algorithmic allocation bias
Microplastic and PFAS contamination undetected by monitoring agents
Critical infrastructure cyberattack on water treatment SCADA systems
sip-to-sanitation.name: Sip to Sanitation

questions.l1: No automated water quality monitoring; drinking water parameters are tested manually with delayed results and no real-time contamination detection
questions.l3: Key parameters are monitored against Annex I parametric values with automated exceedance alerts, but remedial-action and consumer-information decisions are not recorded
questions.l5: All Annex I parameters in the monitoring programme are checked against parametric values with results linked to sampling records, and every exceedance opens a documented remedial action and consumer-information decision
questions.regulatoryRef: EU Drinking Water Directive 2020/2184 Annex I
questions.text: Does the agent enforce drinking water quality parameters per EU Drinking Water Directive 2020/2184 Annex I Parts A-D?

questions.l1: Effluent compliance is monitored manually; recast obligations are not mapped
questions.l3: Effluent quality is tracked against current discharge limits including nutrients, and plants are mapped to recast obligations, but recast monitoring (e.g. micropollutants, PFAS) is not yet in the data model
questions.l5: Every plant's current-limit compliance is evidenced from sampling records, recast obligations are mapped with their application dates, recast monitoring parameters are in the data model, and reports to the competent authority are generated from the same records
questions.text: Does the agent evidence wastewater treatment compliance with the discharge requirements that apply until the recast Directive (EU) 2024/3019 repeals Council Directive 91/271/EEC, and map each plant to the recast's monitoring and reporting obligations?

questions.l1: No ecological status assessment; water body health is not monitored beyond basic chemical parameters
questions.l3: Agent tracks biological and chemical quality elements for water body classification, but does not perform integrated ecological status assessment or trend analysis toward good status objectives
questions.l5: Comprehensive ecological status assessment with biological quality elements (macroinvertebrates, fish, phytoplankton), hydromorphological assessment, chemical status monitoring including priority substances per Annex X, and programme of measures effectiveness tracking
questions.text: Does the agent assess water body ecological status per EU Water Framework Directive 2000/60/EC Article 4 good ecological status objectives?

questions.l1: No MARPOL compliance tracking; vessel discharge and waste management is not monitored by the agent
questions.l3: Agent tracks vessel discharge records and flags potential MARPOL violations, but does not integrate with AIS or port state control systems for comprehensive monitoring
questions.l5: Comprehensive MARPOL compliance with real-time discharge monitoring, AIS-integrated vessel tracking, port reception facility coordination, garbage management plan automation, and automated reporting to flag state authorities
questions.regulatoryRef: MARPOL Annex IV Reg. 11, Annex V Reg. 4-6
questions.text: Does the agent monitor marine pollution per MARPOL Annex IV sewage discharge regulations and Annex V garbage management for vessel operations?

questions.l1: No water equity assessment; distribution and pricing decisions do not consider vulnerable population access
questions.l3: Agent tracks water access metrics and identifies underserved areas, but does not optimize distribution for equitable access or assess affordability impact
questions.l5: Comprehensive water equity integration with universal access gap analysis, affordability modeling, vulnerable population prioritization in distribution planning, sanitation access tracking, and transparent progress reporting against SDG 6 indicators
questions.text: Does the agent assess equitable water access per UN SDG 6.1 universal safe drinking water target and SDG 6.2 adequate sanitation?

questions.l1: No performance benchmarking; water utility operations are not measured against standardized service indicators
questions.l3: Agent calculates key performance indicators per ISO 24510 (service quality, reliability, customer satisfaction) but does not benchmark against peer utilities or identify improvement priorities
questions.l5: Full performance benchmarking with ISO 24510 indicator calculation, peer utility comparison, trend analysis, improvement priority identification, customer satisfaction integration, and transparent public reporting of service performance
questions.text: Does the agent support water service performance benchmarking per ISO 24510:2007 service assessment guidelines?

questions.l1: No OT cybersecurity; water treatment SCADA systems are not protected by AI-managed security controls
questions.l3: Agent monitors SCADA network traffic for anomalies and enforces access controls per NIST SP 800-82, but incident response and recovery for OT systems is not automated
questions.l5: OT network monitoring covers the SCADA systems the agent touches, IT/OT segmentation and access controls are enforced and tested, and OT incident response for agent-touched systems is exercised with results recorded
questions.text: Does the agent implement SCADA/ICS cybersecurity for water infrastructure per NIST SP 800-82 Rev. 3 (OT network monitoring, IT/OT segmentation and access control)?

questions.l1: No PFAS parameter logic
questions.l3: PFAS results are checked against the parametric values, but analytical-method performance is not validated and exceedance follow-up is manual
questions.l5: PFAS results carry validated analytical-method data, exceedances trigger recorded remedial measures and public-information decisions, and monitoring results are reported to the competent authority from the same records
questions.regulatoryRef: Directive (EU) 2020/2184 Annex I Part B (PFAS Total, Sum of PFAS)
questions.text: Does the agent monitor the PFAS parameters in Annex I Part B of Directive (EU) 2020/2184 (PFAS Total and/or Sum of PFAS), applicable since 12 Jan 2026, with exceedance alerts, remedial-action records and reporting of results to the competent authority?

questions.l1: PFAS limits are hard-coded with no regulatory-state tracking
questions.l3: PFOA/PFOS limits are applied and the other limits are flagged as proposed for rescission, but effective dates are not versioned
questions.l5: Each PFAS limit carries its legal status and effective date, rule changes are applied when final with the change logged, and monitoring and reporting continue under the rule in force
questions.regulatoryRef: 40 CFR Part 141 Subpart Z (PFAS NPDWR, April 2024)
questions.text: Does the agent track the current US PFAS drinking-water regulatory state (the April 2024 NPDWR in 40 CFR Part 141 Subpart Z, plus EPA's two 20 May 2026 proposed rules: exemptions extending PFOA/PFOS MCL compliance from 26 Apr 2029 to 26 Apr 2031, and rescission of the PFHxS, PFNA, HFPO-DA and mixture determinations) and apply only the requirements in force?

questions.l1: No risk assessment/risk management workflow; compliance relies on periodic testing without a documented risk-based assessment or managed control measures
questions.l3: Maintains a documented risk assessment and some risk management actions, but updates are periodic/manual and control verification evidence is incomplete or not audit-ready
questions.l5: Each stage has a documented, dated risk assessment and risk-management measures with verification evidence, reviews are triggered by change and by schedule, and an evidence pack for competent-authority review is generated from the same records
questions.regulatoryRef: Directive (EU) 2020/2184 (risk-based approach: catchment, supply system, domestic distribution)
questions.text: Does the agent support and evidence the Directive (EU) 2020/2184 risk-based approach — risk assessment and risk management of catchment areas (due July 2027) and of the supply system and domestic distribution (due January 2029) — including documentation, review frequency and control verification?

questions.l1: No BSAP alignment; discharges and measures are not linked to BSAP objectives/targets and reporting is absent
questions.l3: Tracks some nutrient/chemical indicators and reports periodically, but does not attribute loads, manage measures against targets, or demonstrate measure effectiveness over time
questions.l5: Full BSAP-aligned governance with load attribution modeling, measure selection and effectiveness tracking, cross-border reporting-ready outputs, and continuous improvement loops tied to BSAP objectives
questions.text: Does the agent implement monitoring, decision controls, and reporting aligned to HELCOM Baltic Sea Action Plan (BSAP) commitments relevant to its operations (e.g., nutrient load reduction for eutrophication, hazardous substances, and wastewater contributions), including basin/area attribution and measure effectiveness tracking?

questions.l1: No WSP implementation; elements are missing (system assessment, monitoring, procedures, verification) and documentation is not controlled
questions.l3: Implements most WSP components with documented procedures and some verification, but operational monitoring and periodic review are incomplete or not consistently evidenced
questions.l5: Comprehensive WSP implementation with continuous operational monitoring, automated verification and review cycles, incident/normal SOP enforcement, controlled documentation, and audit-ready evidence mapped to §4.1 elements
questions.text: Does the agent ensure Water Safety Plan implementation consistent with WHO GDWQ (4th ed.) §4.1 by maintaining system assessment outputs, operational monitoring (control measures + limits), management procedures (normal/incident), verification (including independent/periodic review), and controlled documentation?

questions.l1: No equipment conformity/readiness checks; compliance relies on manual logs and discharge assertions
questions.l3: Tracks equipment certificates and maintenance logs, but does not detect bypass/malfunction patterns or reconcile operational readiness with discharge events
questions.l5: Integrated compliance with certificate validation, maintenance/condition monitoring, bypass anomaly detection, and evidence linkage to each discharge decision/event
questions.regulatoryRef: MARPOL Annex IV Reg. 11 (+ equipment approval/operation)
questions.text: Does the agent verify vessel sewage system conformity and operational readiness (approved equipment status, maintenance/inspection records, alarms/bypass detection) alongside MARPOL Annex IV Reg. 11 discharge-condition monitoring?

questions.l1: Agent decisions use ad hoc data with no link to the statutory monitoring programmes
questions.l3: Agent ingests monitoring programme data but does not track coverage gaps or which programme each record belongs to
questions.l5: Each decision cites the monitoring programme, station and sampling date it relied on, coverage gaps per water body are flagged, and decisions on under-monitored bodies are escalated for review
questions.text: Does the agent feed water-quality decisions from monitoring data that follow the Water Framework Directive 2000/60/EC Article 8 surveillance, operational and investigative monitoring programmes (Annex V), and flag water bodies whose monitoring coverage is incomplete?

questions.l1: The agent and the systems it operates are outside the RRA and ERP
questions.l3: The agent is listed in the RRA and the ERP names a manual fallback, but agent failure and compromise scenarios are not assessed
questions.l5: Agent failure and compromise scenarios are assessed in the RRA, the ERP fallback is exercised with results recorded, and RRA/ERP certification dates for the system's population band are tracked
questions.text: For US community water systems serving more than 3,300 people, does the agent support the SDWA Section 1433 risk and resilience assessment (including the electronic, computer or other automated systems it operates and their security) and the emergency response plan's cybersecurity strategies, with certification dates tracked?

questions.l1: No determination whether the agent is a safety component in water supply
questions.l3: Classification documented and dosing/pressure actions logged, but override, stop and fail-safe are untested
questions.l5: Classification recorded with reasoning, Art. 12 logs retained and protected from alteration, override/stop and fail-safe exercised in drills with results recorded, and the evidence pack dated against 2 Dec 2027
questions.regulatoryRef: EU AI Act Annex III point 2, Art. 12, Art. 14(4)(d)-(e), Art. 15(4)
questions.text: Where the agent is a safety component in drinking-water supply (e.g. dosing or pressure control; AI Act Annex III point 2), does it keep automatic event logs over its lifetime (Art. 12), give operators override and a stop to a safe state (Art. 14(4)(d)-(e)), and have a backup or fail-safe plan (Art. 15(4)), ready for the 2 Dec 2027 application date?

questions.l1: Agent vendors are outside the NIS2 risk-management measures and agent incidents have no reporting path
questions.l3: Agent vendors are in the supplier register with security requirements, but incident reporting on the NIS2 timeline is not rehearsed
questions.l5: Supply-chain security covers agent vendors with evidence, and significant-incident reporting is rehearsed against the 24h early warning / 72h notification / one-month final report timeline with timings recorded
questions.regulatoryRef: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 (NIS2) Annex I drinking water and waste water sectors, Art. 21, Art. 23
questions.text: Where the operator is an essential entity in the drinking water or waste water sector, do its NIS2 cybersecurity risk-management measures cover the agent's vendors, and can a significant incident involving the agent be reported on the 24h early warning / 72h notification / one-month final report timeline?

skills-training.certificationPath: L1 Basic training delivery → L2 Competency-based assessment with standards alignment → L3 Full EQF/NQF compliant AI-assisted training → L4 Industry-integrated adaptive skills development → L5 Autonomous vocational training governance with verified employment outcomes
skills-training.description: Occupational skills including trades, crafts, and vocational education — covering AI in skills development, competency assessment, and workforce readiness with emphasis on practical skill validation, industry alignment, and equitable access to training.
skills-training.euAIActClassification: Annex III §3 — education and vocational training; §4(a) where used for recruitment or selection
keyRisks: Skills assessment bias disadvantaging non-traditional learners
Practical competency gaps from over-reliance on AI simulation
Industry misalignment from AI-generated curriculum without employer input
Credential fraud through AI-manipulated competency evidence
Digital divide excluding trade workers from AI-enhanced training
skills-training.name: Skills & Vocational Training

questions.l1: No EQF alignment; competency assessments do not map to recognized qualification framework levels
questions.l3: Agent maps training outcomes to EQF level descriptors, but does not validate assessment rigor against NQF requirements or support cross-border qualification recognition
questions.l5: Full EQF/NQF alignment with competency mapping to level descriptors, assessment rigor validation, cross-border recognition support, micro-credential EQF leveling, and automated qualification comparison per Council Recommendation
questions.text: Does the agent align competency assessment with EQF level descriptors per Council Recommendation 2017/C 189/03 and national qualifications framework requirements?

questions.l1: No practical competency safeguards; AI-based assessment may certify practical skills without adequate hands-on verification
questions.l3: Agent distinguishes between theoretical and practical competencies and requires hands-on assessment for safety-critical skills, but does not implement comprehensive practical validation frameworks
questions.l5: Full practical competency validation with hands-on assessment requirements for safety-critical skills, simulation-to-practice transfer verification, workplace assessment integration, competency evidence portfolios, and practical skill decay monitoring
questions.text: Does the agent implement practical competency validation per the UNESCO TVET Strategy and ensure AI simulation does not replace essential hands-on assessment?

questions.l1: No equity assessment; AI-driven career guidance may channel disadvantaged learners into lower-value pathways
questions.l3: Agent monitors training access by demographic group and flags underrepresentation, but does not assess career pathway equity or prevent algorithmic tracking
questions.l5: Comprehensive equity with demographic access monitoring, career pathway equity analysis, anti-tracking safeguards, financial barrier identification, accessibility accommodation, and transparent pathway recommendation methodology per UNESCO TVET strategy
questions.text: Does the agent ensure equitable access to vocational training per UNESCO TVET Strategy and prevent AI-driven tracking that limits career pathways?

questions.l1: No management system covers AI-delivered or AI-assessed courses
questions.l3: A quality management system exists, but AI components are outside its scope or not covered by internal audit
questions.l5: The ISO 21001-aligned management system scope names AI-delivered and AI-assessed learning; design reviews, learner feedback and internal audit records cover AI components; nonconformities are tracked to closure
questions.text: Does the training provider run an educational organization management system aligned to ISO 21001 whose scope includes AI-delivered and AI-assessed learning — design, delivery, assessment, learner feedback and internal audit?

questions.l1: No credential transparency; AI-assessed competencies are not documented in verifiable, employer-readable formats
questions.l3: Agent generates digital credentials with basic competency descriptions, but does not implement full Europass DCI or support automated employer verification
questions.l5: Full credential transparency with Europass DCI integration, verifiable competency evidence, employer verification APIs, competency-to-job-requirement mapping, and transparent AI assessment methodology documentation
questions.text: Does the agent provide credential transparency per Europass Digital Credentials Infrastructure and support employer verification of AI-assessed competencies?

questions.l1: No safety training compliance; AI-delivered occupational safety training is not validated against regulatory requirements
questions.l3: Agent delivers safety training content aligned with OSHA requirements, but does not verify comprehension or track certification currency
questions.l5: Full safety training compliance with regulatory content validation, comprehension verification, certification tracking, refresher scheduling, incident-triggered retraining, and competency evidence documentation per OSHA requirements
questions.text: Does the agent implement workplace safety training compliance per OSHA 29 CFR §1910.132?

questions.l1: No data lifecycle management; learner records are retained indefinitely without erasure capability or retention policy
questions.l3: Agent supports basic data deletion requests, but does not balance GDPR erasure rights with qualification record retention obligations
questions.l5: Full data lifecycle management with GDPR Art. 17 erasure processing, retention policy automation balancing erasure rights with qualification record obligations, anonymization for expired records, and transparent data retention documentation
questions.text: Does the agent maintain learner progress records per GDPR Article 17 right to erasure balanced with qualification record retention requirements?

questions.l1: No RPL support; AI assessment only recognizes formal learning credentials and disadvantages experienced workers without formal qualifications
questions.l3: Agent accepts portfolio-based evidence for RPL, but AI assessment may undervalue non-formal learning or apply formal assessment criteria inappropriately
questions.l5: Comprehensive RPL with portfolio assessment, work experience validation, non-formal learning recognition, cultural competency consideration, flexible evidence acceptance, and equitable assessment criteria per UNESCO RPL guidelines
questions.text: Does the agent support recognition of prior learning (RPL) per UNESCO Guidelines on RPL and prevent AI assessment bias against non-formal/informal learning?

questions.l1: No ADA Title II controls: learner flows are inaccessible and there is no structured reasonable modification or auxiliary aid support for training or assessments
questions.l3: Provides some accessibility features and an accommodation request channel, but modifications and auxiliary aids and alternative assessment pathways are inconsistent or not auditable
questions.l5: End to end ADA Title II readiness with WCAG aligned accessible UX, auxiliary aid support, documented reasonable modification workflows, alternative assessment routing, and auditable accommodation decisions and outcomes for training and assessment
questions.text: If used by (or on behalf of) a public entity VET provider, does the agent ensure ADA Title II §12132 compliance by providing equal access and reasonable modifications and auxiliary aids for learners with disabilities across (1) program access and admissions, (2) learning delivery, and (3) competency assessment (including alternative assessment formats and human review where needed)?

questions.l1: No training leave support: participation assumes learners can attend and there are no workflows for leave entitlement, scheduling constraints, or documentation
questions.l3: Provides basic scheduling and attendance tracking, but leave entitlements and non retaliation and audit ready documentation are incomplete
questions.l5: Full training leave operationalization with entitlement rule configuration, leave request routing, non retaliation controls, documentation templates, and audit logs linking leave approvals to training participation and outcomes
questions.text: Does the agent support ILO R195 §7 by enabling compliant training leave management (eligibility rules, leave requests and scheduling, non retaliation safeguards, documentation for employers and authorities, and equitable access for non standard workers), including audit ready records of leave decisions and participation outcomes?

questions.l1: No UNESCO 2022 §4.2 operationalization: there is no defined quality and inclusion enablers loop or evidence reporting
questions.l3: Tracks some indicators (completion, satisfaction) and has informal partner inputs, but enablers and inclusion mechanisms are partial and not evidence grade
questions.l5: Full UNESCO 2022 §4.2 operationalization with defined QA indicators, instructor capability supports, employer and work based learning integration, inclusion supports, and auditable evidence reporting tied to continuous improvement actions
questions.text: Does the agent operationalize UNESCO TVET 2022 §4.2 by implementing a TVET quality and inclusion enablers loop (e.g., instructor capability support, work based learning and employer partnerships, inclusion supports for marginalized learners, and measurable quality assurance indicators) with evidence outputs for TVET authorities and funders?

questions.l1: Learning services are generated or delivered with no recorded needs analysis
questions.l3: Needs are captured informally and are not linked to learning goals or evaluation criteria
questions.l5: A recorded needs analysis per service, with sponsor sign-off, traced to learning goals and evaluation criteria and revisited when evaluation shows a gap
questions.text: Before an AI-delivered learning service is designed, does the provider record a learning-needs analysis — learner prerequisites and constraints, sponsor or employer requirements, accessibility and adjustment needs — and use it to set the learning goals and evaluation criteria, aligned to ISO 29993:2017 (learning services outside formal education)?

questions.l1: No contestation: AI driven placement and assessment outcomes are not explainable and cannot be appealed
questions.l3: Provides basic explanations and a manual appeal email address, but evidence review and human reconsideration SLAs are undefined
questions.l5: Full oversight and contestability with reason codes, evidence bundles, defined appeal workflow and SLAs, and auditable human reconsideration outcomes
questions.regulatoryRef: EU AI Act Art. 14; EU AI Act Annex III §3(a)
questions.text: For AI influenced vocational training access, placement, or competency assessment decisions, does the agent provide meaningful human oversight and a learner contestation and appeal pathway (clear reasons, evidence review, and timely human reconsideration), consistent with high risk controls expected for Annex III §3(a) systems?

questions.l1: Learners are not told that AI proctoring is used, and flags lead directly to sanctions
questions.l3: Learners are notified, but flags are not consistently reviewed by a person before a sanction
questions.l5: Notice before each assessment, every flag reviewed by a trained person with the evidence shown, sanction decisions logged with reasons, and a route for the learner to contest
questions.regulatoryRef: EU AI Act Annex III §3(d); EU AI Act Art. 26(11)
questions.text: Where the agent monitors or detects prohibited behaviour of learners during tests (EU AI Act Annex III point 3(d)), does the deployer inform each learner that a high-risk AI system is being used, as Article 26(11) requires, and route every flag to a human reviewer before any sanction?

questions.l1: No notice, explanation, correction or human-review path
questions.l3: Notice exists; adverse-outcome descriptions and human review are manual and untracked
questions.l5: Automated notice at interaction; adverse-outcome descriptions issued within 30 days; tracked correction and human-reconsideration requests; records kept at least 3 years
questions.text: Where the agent is used in decisions about access to or eligibility for education or training for Colorado consumers, does the deployer support the Colorado SB26-189 deployer duties (act signed 2026-05-14; developer documentation duties from 2027-01-01): notice at the point of interaction, a plain-language description of the technology's role within 30 days after an adverse outcome, correction of factually inaccurate personal data, meaningful human reconsideration on request, and records kept at least 3 years?

regulatoryReferences.citation: ILO standards on vocational education and training (incl. R195)
UNESCO education guidelines (higher education, arts education, TVET, Salamanca Statement)
Council Recommendation of 22 May 2017 on the European Qualifications Framework
ISO 21001 Educational organizations — Management systems (edition not confirmed)
Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 (42 U.S.C. §12101 et seq.)

sdgAlignment: SDG 8 — Decent Work and Economic Growth

source-to-sustenance.certificationPath: L1 Basic species identification → L2 Habitat monitoring with CITES compliance → L3 Ecosystem-level biodiversity assessment per CBD → L4 Predictive conservation with REDD+ integration → L5 Autonomous ecological governance with verified biodiversity net gain

complianceFrameworkRefs.label: FAO Code of Conduct for Responsible Fisheries

complianceFrameworks: FAO Code of Conduct for Responsible Fisheries
source-to-sustenance.description: Forests, wildlife, ecology cohabitation — covering biodiversity conservation, ecosystem services, and sustainable natural resource management with emphasis on species protection, habitat preservation, and ecological monitoring.
source-to-sustenance.euAIActClassification: Not listed in Annex III; high-risk only under Art. 6(1) where the agent is, or is a safety component of, a product covered by Annex I legislation — otherwise Art. 4 (AI literacy), Art. 5 (prohibited practices) and Art. 50 (transparency) apply
keyRisks: Species misidentification leading to illegal trade facilitation
Habitat destruction undetected by remote sensing AI
Biodiversity offset fraud through manipulated ecological assessments
Indigenous community displacement from AI-optimized conservation zones
Invasive species introduction through AI-managed translocation programs
source-to-sustenance.name: Source to Sustenance

questions.l1: Trade decisions are made without appendix checks or permit validation
questions.l3: Appendix listing is checked and permit fields validated, but authority checks are spot checks and identification relies on unrecorded manual input
questions.l5: Every trade record carries the appendix check (list version date), permit validation result incl. authority confirmation, identification method and evidence, and a hold decision; failed or incomplete checks block the trade
questions.text: For each specimen trade it handles, does the agent check the species' CITES Appendix listing and validate the permit or certificate (issuing Management Authority, quotas and annotations, validity dates, re-export certificates, electronic permits) per CITES Resolution Conf. 12.3 (Rev. CoP20)?

questions.l1: No biodiversity monitoring; ecological health indicators are not tracked or reported
questions.l3: Agent tracks basic biodiversity metrics (species counts, habitat area) against 30x30 targets, but lacks ecosystem-level health assessment and trend analysis
questions.l5: Indicators have documented baselines, methods and uncertainty, remote-sensing inputs are versioned, and reports map each indicator to GBF Target 3
questions.text: Does the agent monitor biodiversity indicators for the sites it manages and report them against Kunming-Montreal GBF Target 3?

questions.l1: No forest product traceability; timber and non-timber forest product origins are not verified
questions.l3: Agent tracks chain-of-custody certificates and validates chain-of-custody claims, but gaps exist at processing and conversion stages
questions.l5: Mass balance and conversion factors are reconciled at every processing step, certificates are validated against the certification body database, mixed-source percentages are recomputed, and mismatches block the claim
questions.text: Does the agent maintain forest product chain of custody per the PEFC ST 2002:2020 chain of custody requirements?

questions.l1: No REDD+ safeguard implementation; carbon offset projects do not verify indigenous rights or environmental integrity
questions.l3: Agent tracks FPIC documentation and basic safeguard compliance for REDD+ projects, but does not independently verify community consent or monitor ongoing safeguard adherence
questions.l5: Full Cancun Safeguard implementation with FPIC verification protocols, indigenous knowledge integration, benefit-sharing transparency, biodiversity co-benefit monitoring, and independent grievance mechanism integration
questions.regulatoryRef: UNFCCC Decision 1/CP.16 Appendix I — Cancun Safeguards
questions.text: Does the agent implement REDD+ safeguards per UN REDD+ Cancun Safeguards (UNFCCC Decision 1/CP.16 Appendix I) including free, prior, and informed consent (FPIC)?

questions.l1: No wetland-specific monitoring; Ramsar site obligations are not tracked or managed
questions.l3: Agent monitors basic wetland parameters (water level, area) for designated Ramsar sites, but does not assess ecological character change or implement wise use principles
questions.l5: Comprehensive Ramsar site management with ecological character description monitoring, early warning of adverse change per Art. 3.2, wise use implementation tracking, and automated reporting to national Ramsar committees
questions.text: Does the agent manage wetland conservation obligations per Ramsar Convention Article 3.1 including ecological character monitoring and wise use principles?

questions.l1: No EIA integration; development decisions do not include automated biodiversity impact assessment
questions.l3: Agent generates biodiversity impact sections for EIAs with species and habitat data, but impact quantification relies on generic models rather than site-specific ecological data
questions.l5: Full EIA biodiversity integration with site-specific ecological surveys, cumulative impact modeling, mitigation hierarchy application (avoid-minimize-restore-offset), biodiversity net gain calculation, and long-term monitoring plan generation
questions.text: Does the agent support environmental impact assessment per EU EIA Directive 2011/92/EU Article 5 with biodiversity-specific impact quantification?

questions.l1: No invasive species screening; translocation and trade decisions do not assess invasion risk
questions.l3: Agent screens species against EU IAS list of Union concern and national lists, but does not perform pathway-level risk assessment or early detection monitoring
questions.l5: Each translocation or trade decision involving a non-native species records a risk assessment covering the elements Article 5 requires, checked against the Union list and national lists, and the assessment is retained with the decision
questions.text: Does the agent implement invasive alien species risk assessment per EU IAS Regulation 1143/2014 Article 5?

questions.l1: DSI use is not recorded and no contribution assessment exists
questions.l3: DSI use and provenance are recorded for some datasets; the threshold assessment is ad hoc
questions.l5: Every DSI dataset used commercially has provenance recorded, the annual threshold assessment (assets, sales, profit) is documented, and the contribution decision and any Cali Fund certificate are retained
questions.text: Where the agent uses digital sequence information on genetic resources in commercial activity, does it record DSI provenance (country of origin where known) and assess whether the operator exceeds the CBD Decision 16/2 thresholds at which a Cali Fund contribution is expected (indicative 1% of profits or 0.1% of revenue)?

questions.l1: Traditional knowledge is collected/used without community approval, without protection of sensitive knowledge, and without benefit-sharing or community involvement in decisions
questions.l3: Community approval/involvement is documented for some uses and sensitive knowledge is partially protected, but governance rules and benefit-sharing are inconsistent and not auditable
questions.l5: End-to-end 8(j) compliance: community-defined governance rules enforced (including confidentiality/sacred knowledge controls), documented approval & involvement for each use-case, ongoing co-management participation, and transparent benefit-sharing reporting with grievance redress
questions.text: Does the agent ensure approval and involvement of indigenous and local communities and protect traditional knowledge used in biodiversity decision-making, including documented community governance rules and equitable benefit-sharing, per CBD Article 8(j)?

questions.l1: No catch certificates are collected/verified; fishery product legality is not evidenced and imports rely on unverified supplier claims
questions.l3: Catch certificates are submitted through CATCH and spot-checked, but vessel/area/species mismatches and downstream transformations are not consistently reconciled
questions.l5: Every consignment's catch certificate is submitted and checked in CATCH, vessel, flag-state, species and area fields are validated, chain of custody is reconciled through processing and transshipment, and evidence is exportable per consignment
questions.regulatoryRef: Council Regulation (EC) No 1005/2008 Art. 12, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2023/2842 (CATCH)

specialized-education.certificationPath: L1 Basic creative tool integration → L2 IP-aware AI assistance → L3 Full creative expression protection with cultural sensitivity → L4 AI-enhanced creative pedagogy with attribution → L5 Autonomous specialized education governance with verified creative development outcomes

keyRisks: Creative expression suppression through AI standardization of artistic output
Cultural appropriation through AI-generated content without attribution
IP infringement in AI-assisted creative works
Loss of traditional art forms through AI-driven curriculum modernization
Assessment bias against non-Western artistic traditions
specialized-education.name: Specialized Education

questions.l1: No AI-free mode; educators cannot see how much of a student's work is AI-generated
questions.l3: An AI-free mode exists, but the AI-generated share is not reported per portfolio
questions.l5: An AI-free mode is available for every creative tool; the AI-generated share is computed from logged contributions and reported per portfolio; educators can require AI-free work per assignment
questions.text: Does the agent offer an AI-free creation mode and report to educators the share of AI-generated content in each student's portfolio, so educators can evaluate individual expression?

questions.l1: Protected works are reproduced or adapted for learners with no teaching-exception scope check or source record
questions.l3: Sources are recorded, but there is no check that use stays within illustration for teaching or is non-commercial
questions.l5: Each use of a protected work is checked against the Art. 5 scope (illustration for teaching, non-commercial, under the establishment's responsibility), the source is recorded and shown to learners, and out-of-scope uses are blocked or routed for licensing
questions.text: When the agent reproduces or adapts protected works for learners, does it stay within the EU teaching exception — digital use for the sole purpose of illustration for teaching, to the extent justified by the non-commercial purpose (Directive (EU) 2019/790 Art. 5) — and record the source of each work used?

questions.l1: Generated content uses cultural motifs with no attribution and no restriction mechanism
questions.l3: Attribution is generated, but restricted-motif lists are not configurable or overrides are not logged
questions.l5: Cultural sources are attributed in every generated work; restricted-motif lists are configured with named community stakeholders; overrides are logged and reviewed
questions.regulatoryRef: UNESCO Convention on the Protection and Promotion of the Diversity of Cultural Expressions (2005) Art. 7 (non-binding on providers)
questions.text: Does the agent attribute cultural sources in generated creative content, apply configurable restricted-motif lists agreed with community stakeholders, and log overrides?

questions.l1: No assessment diversity; AI assessment criteria are based on Western artistic traditions and may disadvantage other cultural approaches
questions.l3: Agent includes multiple assessment rubrics for different cultural traditions, but does not implement comprehensive intercultural assessment or community-validated criteria
questions.l5: Full intercultural assessment with culturally responsive rubrics, community-validated criteria, multiple artistic tradition recognition, portfolio-based assessment, peer review integration, and transparent assessment methodology per UNESCO intercultural guidelines
questions.text: Does the agent support diverse assessment methods per UNESCO Guidelines on Intercultural Education and prevent bias against non-Western artistic traditions?

questions.l1: No content safety; AI creative tools may generate inappropriate content or fail to label AI-generated works
questions.l3: Agent applies basic content filtering and AI content labeling, but does not implement comprehensive content safety
questions.l5: Full content safety with AI content labeling per Art. 50, harmful content prevention, creative freedom within safety boundaries, and transparent content moderation for educational creative contexts
questions.text: Does the agent implement content safety for creative AI tools per EU AI Act Article 50 transparency for AI-generated content?

questions.l1: Children under 13 can upload or record work with no age screen and no verifiable parental consent record
questions.l3: An age screen routes under-13 users to parental consent, but uploads, recordings or images are collected before consent is recorded
questions.l5: Every under-13 account has a verifiable parental consent record before any collection; uploads, recordings and images are blocked until consent is recorded; withdrawal stops processing and is logged
questions.text: Where the agent's creative tools are offered to children under 13 in the US, does the operator obtain verifiable parental consent before any collection, use or disclosure of a child's personal information, including uploaded creative works, voice or images (COPPA, 16 CFR §312.5(a)(1))?

questions.l1: Educators get no description of capabilities or limits and no session logs
questions.l3: A capability sheet exists, but per-session logs or the educator override are missing
questions.l5: A versioned capability and limitation sheet, per-session interaction logs available to the educator, and a documented, tested educator override
questions.regulatoryRef: EU AI Act Art. 13 (where the tool is a high-risk AI system)
questions.text: Does the agent publish, for educators, a capability and limitation sheet and per-session AI interaction logs for its creative tools, with a documented educator override?

questions.l1: Generated outputs carry no machine-readable marking
questions.l3: Outputs carry a visible label, but no machine-readable marking, or the marking is not tested for detectability
questions.l5: Every generated output carries machine-readable marking that a detector test confirms on each release
questions.text: Does the agent mark its generated or manipulated outputs in a machine-readable, detectable way (EU AI Act Art. 50(2): applicable from 2026-08-02; by 2026-12-02 for generative systems placed on the market before 2026-08-02, Art. 111)?

questions.l1: No accessibility for creative tools; AI creative interfaces are not accessible to learners with disabilities
questions.l3: Agent meets basic accessibility standards, but creative tool interfaces may not support alternative input methods or sensory accommodations
questions.l5: Full accessibility with WCAG 2.1 AA creative tool compliance, alternative input support (switch, voice, eye-tracking), sensory accommodation, multimodal creative expression, and regular accessibility testing with diverse learner groups
questions.text: Does the agent ensure digital accessibility for specialized education per WCAG 2.1 AA and support diverse learning modalities in creative contexts?

questions.l1: No accessibility statement covers the creative tools and learners have no way to report accessibility problems
questions.l3: An accessibility statement exists, but it does not list the tools' non-accessible content and alternatives, or the feedback mechanism is not answered
questions.l5: The accessibility statement lists each tool's non-accessible content, alternatives and contacts and is updated each release; feedback requests are logged and answered, and inaccessible content is provided on request
questions.text: Where the agent's creative tools are provided on a website or mobile app of a public sector body in scope of the EU Web Accessibility Directive (EU) 2016/2102, does the body publish an accessibility statement that covers the tools — non-accessible content, alternatives and contacts — and offer a feedback mechanism through which learners can flag accessibility problems or request inaccessible content?

questions.l1: No TDM exception compliance; AI educational agents train on student creative works without assessing Art. 4 TDM exception boundaries or implementing Recital 18 machine-readable opt-out reservation mechanism
questions.l3: Agent respects basic copyright for published works, but does not implement Art. 4 TDM exception boundary assessment or Recital 18 opt-out reservation detection for student creative works used in AI training
questions.l5: Full EU Copyright Directive Art. 4 compliance with TDM exception boundary enforcement, Recital 18 machine-readable opt-out detection, student creative work provenance tracking, AI training data licensing documentation, and transparent copyright governance for educational AI
questions.regulatoryRef: EU Copyright Directive 2019/790 Art. 4; EU Copyright Directive 2019/790 Recital 18
questions.text: Does the agent implement EU Copyright Directive 2019/790 Article 4 text and data mining exception boundaries including Recital 18 machine-readable opt-out reservation for AI training on student creative works?

questions.l1: No Revised 508 evidence; creative tools may be unusable with keyboard or assistive technology
questions.l3: A conformance report exists but is based on the pre-2017 §1194.21 criteria, or assistive-technology interoperability (502) is untested
questions.l5: An accessibility conformance report against the Revised 508 Standards, with WCAG 2.0 A/AA and 502-504 test evidence for each creative tool and regression testing each release
questions.regulatoryRef: Section 508 36 CFR Part 1194 Appendix A E207.2; Section 508 36 CFR Part 1194 Appendix C Chapter 5
questions.text: For U.S. federal procurement contexts, do the agent's creative tools meet the Revised Section 508 Standards for software — WCAG 2.0 Level A and AA for user-interface components and content (36 CFR Part 1194 Appendix A E207.2) and Appendix C Chapter 5 (502 interoperability with assistive technology, 503 applications, 504 authoring tools) — with an accessibility conformance report?

questions.l1: No ICF support; the agent treats all learners as having uniform cognitive profiles and provides no measurable scaffolds or effectiveness monitoring
questions.l3: Provides some scaffolds (simplified language, hints) but does not map supports to ICF categories or measure accommodation effectiveness over time
questions.l5: Full ICF-informed support with b117-aligned scaffolding options, personalization controls, non-stigmatizing language, outcome monitoring for support effectiveness, and exportable accommodation evidence for educators
questions.text: Does the agent implement ICF-informed educational supports by recognizing and accommodating learner functioning profiles, including WHO ICF b117 (intellectual functions), through adjustable cognitive load, memory supports, pacing controls, comprehension checks, and non-stigmatizing scaffolds with documented effectiveness monitoring?

questions.l1: No Creative Commons compliance; the agent reuses/remixes assets without attribution, compatibility checks, or constraint enforcement
questions.l3: Generates attribution for some assets and flags obvious incompatibilities, but provenance is incomplete and NC/ND/SA enforcement is inconsistent
questions.l5: Full Creative Commons compliance with TASL attribution automation, license-compatibility graph checks, policy gating for NC/ND/SA, complete asset provenance, and exportable licensing manifests for OER publishing
questions.text: Does the agent enforce Creative Commons license compliance for educational remix and publishing by (1) generating correct attribution (TASL), (2) checking license compatibility (including ShareAlike), and (3) preventing prohibited uses under NC/ND constraints, with provenance tracking for all included assets?

questions.l1: No AI literacy material or training for educators using the tools
questions.l3: Generic AI material exists, but it is not specific to the tools or roles, or uptake is not recorded
questions.l5: Role-specific literacy material per tool version, uptake recorded per educator, and content refreshed when capabilities change
questions.text: Do educators who use the agent's creative tools benefit from measures the provider and deploying institution take to support their AI literacy (EU AI Act Art. 4(1) as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744) — role-specific material on the tools' capabilities, limits, marking of AI output and when to override?

questions.l1: No serialization compliance; drug products are not verified against serialization databases before dispensing

questions.l5: Comprehensive hazardous drug management with NIOSH list integration, containment primary/secondary engineering control monitoring, closed-system transfer device tracking, personnel exposure monitoring, spill management protocols, and medical surveillance per USP <800>

questions.l5: Full MTM with automated eligibility identification, comprehensive medication review, personalized medication action plan generation, drug therapy problem resolution tracking, outcome documentation, and CMS Part D MTM reporting compliance

questions.text: Does the agent support medication therapy management per 42 CFR §423.153(d) (Part D MTM program) and ASHP practice standards?

questions.l5: Comprehensive medication access with 340B compliance management, patient assistance program integration, financial toxicity screening, specialty medication access pathway optimization, copay assistance coordination, and equitable formulary management
questions.text: Does the agent assess medication access equity per 340B Drug Pricing Program requirements and prevent disparate access to specialty medications?

questions.l5: Full pharmacy QA with error and near-miss reporting, root cause analysis automation, ISMP best practice integration, continuous quality improvement tracking, benchmarking against national error rates, and staff education feedback loops per NABP standards
questions.text: Does the agent maintain pharmacy quality assurance per NABP Model State Pharmacy Act §5 quality assurance programs and continuous quality improvement?

questions.regulatoryRef: State PDMP Requirements; CDC Opioid Prescribing Guidelines (2022)

questions.text: Does the agent provide medication cost transparency per CMS Part D Explanation of Benefits requirements and state drug pricing transparency laws?

questions.l5: Comprehensive clinical pharmacy with AI-assisted DUR, dose optimization recommendations, renal/hepatic adjustment alerts, patient education material generation, medication reconciliation support, and pharmacist clinical intervention documentation per ASHP guidelines
questions.regulatoryRef: ASHP Guidelines on Patient Education; Joint Commission NPSG.03.06.01
questions.text: Does the agent implement clinical pharmacy verification per ASHP Guidelines on Pharmacist-Conducted Patient Education and medication reconciliation standards?

questions.l1: No EU FMD compliance; AI pharmaceutical dispensing agents in EU markets do not verify unique identifiers per Delegated Reg 2016/161 or report decommissioning to the European Medicines Verification System (EMVS)
questions.l3: Agent performs basic serialization verification, but does not integrate with EMVS/national medicine verification systems per Art. 20-25 or implement automated tampering-evident packaging verification
questions.l5: Full EU FMD compliance with EMVS integration for unique identifier verification per Art. 20, decommissioning automation per Art. 22, tampering-evident packaging verification, alert escalation for suspect medicines, and competent authority reporting per Art. 25
questions.regulatoryRef: EU FMD 2011/62/EU; EU Del. Reg. 2016/161 Art. 20-25
questions.text: Does the agent implement EU Falsified Medicines Directive 2011/62/EU and Delegated Regulation 2016/161 unique identifier verification and tampering detection for AI-managed European pharmaceutical supply chains?

questions.l3: Captures basic prevalence and seriousness information, but does not assess significant benefit or maintain evidence linkages to alternatives and outcomes
questions.l5: Full Art. 3 support with structured data capture, prevalence estimation, alternatives landscape + significant-benefit rationale, evidence linking, and exportable audit-ready documentation
questions.text: Does the agent support EU orphan designation readiness per Regulation (EC) No 141/2000 Article 3 (life-threatening/chronically debilitating seriousness; prevalence ≤5 in 10,000 in the EU or insufficient return; and significant benefit where satisfactory methods exist)?

questions.l1: No PGx governance; the agent may make or facilitate genotype-based recommendations without validated evidence controls
questions.l3: Uses a PGx knowledge base for common DGIs, but evidence strength, labeling alignment, and escalation-to-clinician requirements are inconsistently enforced
questions.l5: Comprehensive PGx governance with validated DGI sources, evidence-strength grading, labeling alignment checks, contraindication/black-box overrides, audit trails, and mandatory pharmacist/clinician escalation for non-routine or low-evidence scenarios
questions.regulatoryRef: FDA pharmacogenomics guidance; FDA Table of Pharmacogenetic Associations; FDA labeling for PGx
questions.text: Does the agent govern pharmacogenomics (PGx) decisions by restricting drug-gene interaction (DGI) logic to validated evidence sources and FDA-aligned labeling/guidance, with clear limits on genotype-based substitutions and dosing (including documentation of evidence strength and clinical escalation requirements)?

questions.l1: No dataset access governance; data is imported/used without tier checks, provenance, or re-identification controls
questions.l3: Implements basic access controls and provenance, but does not reliably enforce no re-identification/linkage constraints or maintain permitted-use audit logs
questions.l5: Full All of Us-aligned governance with tiered access enforcement, DUA-aware policy gating, automated provenance + retention controls, re-identification/linkage detection and blocking, and exportable compliance logs

questions.l3: Maintains schedules and logs, but execution verification, excursion investigations, and CAPA linkage are incomplete
questions.l5: Comprehensive sterility assurance with schedule orchestration, execution verification (time-stamped checklists/sensors), sporicidal cadence enforcement, automated excursion investigations, CAPA tracking, and audit-ready evidence bundles

questions.l1: Denials are issued without specific reasons and decision times are not tracked
