Addiction to AI wellness coaching creating dependency rather than autonomy
wellness-management.name: Wellness Management

questions.l1: No crisis detection or protocol; the agent can be mistaken for a human
questions.l3: Crisis keywords trigger hotline information and an AI disclosure exists, but the protocol is unpublished, untested, or has no human escalation path
questions.l5: A documented protocol with human escalation is published where required; detection and referral are tested per release with recorded results; referral notifications are counted (Cal. reporting from 1 Jul 2027)
questions.regulatoryRef: SAMHSA National Guidelines for Behavioral Health Crisis Care; Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code §§22601-22603
questions.text: Does the agent detect suicidal ideation and self-harm content and follow a documented crisis protocol with referral to crisis services (SAMHSA National Guidelines), and, where it is a companion chatbot under Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code §22601, disclose that it is AI and publish its protocol (§22602)?

questions.l1: No special category data protections; wellness data including mental health, biometrics, and health conditions processed without explicit consent differentiation
questions.l3: Agent obtains explicit consent for special category data processing and maintains consent records, but does not implement granular purpose limitation or automated consent withdrawal processing
questions.l5: Full GDPR Art. 9 compliance with granular explicit consent per processing purpose, automated consent withdrawal with cascading data deletion, purpose limitation enforcement, special category data minimization, and transparent processing documentation per Art. 30
questions.text: Does the agent enforce GDPR Article 9(2)(a) explicit consent for processing special category health and biometric wellness data?

questions.l1: The agent gives weight-loss or restriction advice with no screening for risk indicators
questions.l3: Extreme recommendations are filtered by templates, but risk indicators in free text are not detected or not routed
questions.l5: Output filters and indicator detection are tested with a red-team set per release; flagged users get a referral message and no further restriction advice; results are logged and reviewed
questions.regulatoryRef: NICE NG69 Eating disorders: recognition and treatment
questions.text: Does the agent avoid producing restrictive dieting or body-weight content that could trigger eating disorders, and route users who show eating-disorder indicators to professional assessment rather than giving advice, consistent with NICE NG69 recognition and referral recommendations?

questions.l1: No data separation; employer-sponsored wellness data is accessible to HR/management without de-identification
questions.l3: Agent separates individual wellness data from employer-accessible aggregate reports, but does not prevent re-identification through small group analytics or temporal correlation
questions.l5: Individual data is stored separately from employer-accessible systems; employer reports are aggregate with a documented minimum group size; a re-identification review is run before new report types; participation is voluntary and evidenced
questions.text: For employer-sponsored wellness programs, does the agent keep individual wellness data separate from the employer and release only aggregate reports (ADA 42 U.S.C. §12112(d)(4)(B); 29 CFR 1630.14(d)(4))?

questions.l1: Recommendations include unsubstantiated health claims
questions.l3: Major claims reference evidence, but the evidence is not graded or limits are not disclosed
questions.l5: Every health-benefit claim template links to its substantiating evidence with grade and date; claims without adequate evidence are blocked; evidence links are reviewed on a schedule
questions.regulatoryRef: FTC Act 15 U.S.C. §45; FTC Health Products Compliance Guidance
questions.text: Does the agent make health-benefit claims for wellness interventions only when supported by competent and reliable scientific evidence (FTC Act §5; FTC Health Products Compliance Guidance), and state evidence limits to users?

questions.l1: No algorithmic transparency; wellness scores and recommendations are black-box with no explanation of factors or methodology
questions.l3: Agent provides basic explanations of wellness score components and recommendation rationale, but does not offer detailed factor weighting or allow users to understand how their data influences outputs
questions.l5: Full algorithmic transparency with detailed factor explanation, individual feature contribution visualization, counterfactual explanations, user-accessible methodology documentation, and regular bias auditing per EU AI Act Art. 13 requirements
questions.text: Does the agent provide algorithmic transparency for wellness scoring and recommendations per EU AI Act Article 13 transparency obligations?

questions.l1: No OH&S integration; occupational wellness does not connect to workplace hazard identification or risk assessment
questions.l3: Agent tracks workplace wellness indicators and correlates with reported hazards per Clause 6.1.2, but does not proactively identify emerging occupational health risks or recommend hierarchy of controls
questions.l5: Comprehensive OH&S integration with proactive hazard identification from wellness data patterns, hierarchy of controls recommendations per Clause 8.1.2, worker consultation facilitation per Clause 7.4, and continuous improvement tracking per Clause 10.3
questions.text: Does the agent manage occupational health and safety per ISO 45001:2018 Clause 6.1.2 hazard identification and Clause 8.1.2 eliminating hazards?

questions.l1: No insurance discrimination prevention; wellness data could be accessed or inferred by insurance underwriters
questions.l3: Agent restricts direct data sharing with insurers, but does not prevent indirect inference through aggregated wellness program participation data or third-party data broker access
questions.l5: Full discrimination prevention with data isolation from insurance systems, inference attack prevention, third-party data broker monitoring, automated discrimination risk assessment, and transparent data flow documentation proving no insurance underwriting pathway exists
questions.text: Does the agent prevent wellness data from being used for insurance underwriting discrimination per GINA Title I and ACA §1201 pre-existing condition protections?

questions.l1: No log of recommendations; outputs name conditions or give treatment advice while marketed as wellness
questions.l3: Recommendations are logged and templates avoid disease naming, but free-text outputs are not tested against the boundary
questions.l5: All outputs are logged; a boundary test set runs on each release with recorded results; boundary failures block release; HCP-referral wording is reviewed against the guidance
questions.regulatoryRef: FDA General Wellness: Policy for Low Risk Devices (January 2026)
questions.text: Does the agent log every recommendation and notification it issues and test them against FDA's General Wellness policy (January 2026), so that wellness outputs do not name a disease or condition, apply clinical thresholds, or give diagnoses or treatment recommendations?

questions.l1: No data portability; users cannot export their wellness data in a structured, machine-readable format
questions.l3: Agent supports basic data export in CSV/PDF format, but does not provide FHIR-formatted health data or support automated transfer to other wellness/health platforms
questions.l5: Full data portability with FHIR-formatted wellness data export, automated platform-to-platform transfer, Apple Health/Google Fit integration, comprehensive data package including all derived insights, and portability request processing within GDPR Art. 20 timeline
questions.text: Does the agent implement data portability for wellness records per GDPR Article 20 right to data portability and FHIR-based health data exchange?

questions.l1: Workplace emotion inference is available with no legal analysis
questions.l3: Emotion features are disabled by configuration, but there is no test evidence, worker notice record or log-retention setting
questions.l5: Emotion inference is technically blocked outside documented medical or safety exceptions and tested; worker notices are recorded before use; logs are retained at least six months where Art. 26(6) applies (high-risk obligations apply from 2 Dec 2027 per Regulation (EU) 2026/1744)
questions.regulatoryRef: EU AI Act Art. 5(1)(f); EU AI Act Art. 26(6)-(7)
questions.text: If an employer deploys the wellness agent, does it refuse to infer workers' emotions except for medical or safety reasons (EU AI Act Art. 5(1)(f)), and, where the system is high-risk, keep its logs (Art. 26(6)) and inform workers and their representatives before use (Art. 26(7))?

questions.l1: Wellness scores/flags are used to automatically make consequential decisions (eligibility, benefits, access) with no human review or contest mechanism
questions.l3: Provides human review on request and basic explanation, but consequential decisions can still be executed by default from automated scoring and contest timelines are unclear
questions.l5: Default human-in-the-loop for consequential decisions, clear non-solely-automated routing, robust contest workflow with SLAs, meaningful explanation of key factors, and documented assessment of `similarly significant effect` for each decision pathway
questions.regulatoryRef: GDPR Art. 22(1) (and safeguards per Art. 22(3), Arts. 13–15)
questions.text: Does the agent prevent solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects based on wellness/health data by implementing GDPR Art. 22(1) safeguards (human review, ability to contest, and meaningful information about the logic for any consequential scoring/eligibility decisions)?

questions.l1: No breach-notice workflow; incidents are handled ad hoc and required notices are missed or incomplete
questions.l3: Has an incident playbook and can generate draft notices, but cannot reliably determine HBNR applicability, track timing, or ensure required notice contents and delivery
questions.l5: Automated HBNR applicability triage, evidence-backed incident timeline, notice templating meeting §318.6 content requirements, delivery tracking, and audit-ready logs of all notifications and determinations
questions.text: Does the agent support FTC Health Breach Notification Rule compliance by detecting `breaches of security` involving identifiable health information and executing end-to-end notification workflows (timely notice, required contents, and recipient-specific routing) per 16 CFR Part 318, including §318.6?

questions.l1: Core flows are not accessible (e.g., screen-reader issues, inaccessible forms), and no accommodation pathway exists
questions.l3: Meets baseline accessibility checks and provides some accommodations, but coverage is inconsistent (chat, charts, videos, consent flows) and no systematic regression testing exists
questions.l5: End-to-end accessible wellness experience with verified accessibility across all critical flows (onboarding/consent, crisis escalation, dashboards), documented accommodation policy, accessibility regression testing, and effective-communication support for assistive technologies
questions.text: Does the agent ensure non-discriminatory access to wellness services for users with disabilities by meeting ADA Title III §12182 obligations (reasonable modifications, effective communication/auxiliary aids, and accessible digital interaction flows)?

questions.l1: No high-risk AI lifecycle controls; limited documentation, weak logging, and no defined human oversight for consequential outputs
questions.l3: Maintains partial documentation and some logging, but risk management and data governance are incomplete and conformity evidence is fragmented
questions.l5: Classification record shows whether 5(a)/5(c) applies; where it does, risk management, data governance, logging, human oversight and technical documentation exist and map to Arts. 9-15, ready before 2 Dec 2027
questions.regulatoryRef: EU AI Act Annex III point 5(a), 5(c); EU AI Act Arts. 9-15; Regulation (EU) 2026/1744
questions.text: If the wellness system is used by or for public authorities to evaluate eligibility for healthcare services (EU AI Act Annex III point 5(a)) or for life and health insurance risk assessment and pricing (point 5(c)), does its provider implement the high-risk controls of Arts. 9-15 with conformity evidence, applicable from 2 December 2027?

questions.l1: No design controls; requirements, V&V, and change impacts are undocumented or inconsistent
questions.l3: Has documented requirements and some testing, but design reviews, validation evidence, and change-control traceability are incomplete
questions.l5: Full ISO 13485-aligned design controls with traceable requirements, design reviews, verification/validation protocols, release gates, design transfer controls, and design-change impact analysis with auditable records
questions.text: If the wellness agent includes medical-like intervention selection/monitoring features, does the development and change process follow ISO 13485:2016 §7.3 design & development controls (planning, inputs, outputs, review, verification, validation, transfer, and change control)?

questions.l1: No DPIA for large-scale wellness data processing
questions.l3: A DPIA exists but predates the agent or does not cover its data flows (model endpoints, tools, logs)
questions.l5: A DPIA covers the agent's data flows, is approved before processing, is reviewed on material change, and its mitigations are traced to implemented controls
questions.text: Before an employer or provider processes workers' or users' wellness data on a large scale through the agent, is a GDPR Art. 35 data protection impact assessment completed and kept current?
